Press **Refresh** to read your brokers, Message VPNs and pages from the gateway again. It does not sign you out and does not reload the page. Use it after an administrator has changed what you may use. The pages in the sidebar change to match.

If the gateway cannot be reached, the card shows the reason and keeps the list you had. If your session has ended, you return to the **Sign in** card.

### Switching to another Message VPN

There are two ways.

- Press **Disconnect**, choose the other Message VPN in the Connect card and press **Connect**. Both connections open again.
- Pick a queue that lives on another Message VPN from the queue list of Queue Browser or Queue Copy. The app asks `Current VPN is "default". Switch to "billing"?` Press **Switch** to continue, or **Cancel** to stay as you are. On **Switch** the messaging connection closes and opens again on the other Message VPN, and SEMP stays up. The page you came from then opens with the queue.

If you are not connected when you pick such a queue, the app takes you to the Connect card and you choose the broker and Message VPN yourself.

A switch that cannot finish leaves the reason on the Connect card and in a warning that begins `Could not switch to VPN "billing":` and then gives the reason. The reasons are:

- `the session on VPN "default" did not close within 10 s.`
- `VPN "billing" did not connect within 30 s.`
- `the connection to VPN "billing" closed before it came up.`
- `Messaging (client):` followed by the reason of a failed connect, as in the table above. SEMP is closed too, because the connection is one connection. Press **Connect** to start again.

While a connect is running, a request to switch is refused with `A connection attempt is in progress. Try again once it has finished.`

### Disconnecting and signing out

- **Disconnect** closes both connections and returns to the Connect card. You stay signed in.
- **Sign out** is the last icon of the account control. It closes your connection if there is one, ends your session on the gateway and returns the tab to the **Sign in** card. The sidebar's account control goes away.

### Changing your password

Press **Change password**, the key icon at the top of the sidebar. It opens the gateway's own page. The page is a link away from the app, so leaving it closes your connection. Press **Connect** again when you return.

1. Type your **Current password**.
2. Type the **New password** twice: in **New password** and in **Confirm new password**. The page says how long it may be, as `N to 128 characters`. Your administrator sets the shortest length.
3. Press **Change password**. You return to the app and stay signed in here. Any other browser you were signed in on is signed out.

Press **Cancel** to leave without changing anything. When the gateway insists on a change first, the page says `You must set a new password before you continue.` and has no **Cancel**.

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `The current password is not correct.` | Type your current password again. A wrong password counts like a failed sign-in. |
| `The new passwords do not match.` | Type the same text in both new-password boxes. |
| `The new password must be N to 128 characters.` | Choose one of a length the page allows. |
| `The new password must differ from the current one.` | Choose a different password. |
| `Too many attempts. Try again in N seconds.` | Wait as long as the message says. |
| `The password could not be checked. Try again.` or `The password could not be saved.` | Nothing changed. Try again, and tell your administrator if it repeats. |
| `Your account was changed while this request ran. Sign in again.` | Sign in again, then repeat the change. |
| `The gateway cannot record changes right now, so it refused this one. Try again later or tell an administrator.` | Nothing changed. Try again later. |

### Two-factor sign-in

Two-factor sign-in asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone after your password. Your administrator decides whether it is optional, required for administrators, or required for everyone. Whatever the rule, you can set it up yourself, and once it is on, the gateway always asks for a code.

#### Setting it up

When the gateway requires it of you and you have not set it up, the sign-in carries on to the page **Set up two-factor sign-in** after your password, and you are not signed in until you finish. Start at step 2 below. To set it up of your own accord, press **Two-factor sign-in**, the lock icon at the top of the sidebar.

1. On the page **Two-factor sign-in**, type your **Password**. If two-factor is already on, also type **Current code or a recovery code**. Press **Continue**. **Cancel** leaves without changing anything.
2. On **Set up two-factor sign-in**, scan the picture with an authenticator app. Or type the **Key** shown under it into the app. If the picture cannot be drawn, the page says `The picture could not be drawn. Type the key into your app instead.`
3. Type the six-digit code the app shows in **Code** and press **Turn on two-factor sign-in**.
4. The page **Recovery codes** lists ten codes in groups of four characters. Save them somewhere other than your phone. Each works once, and this page is the only place they are shown. Press **Continue**. If you must also choose a new password, **Continue** takes you to that page first.

> [!WARNING]
> The recovery codes are shown only once. If you lose your phone and have no recovery code left, only an administrator can reset your two-factor sign-in. You cannot turn it off yourself, and your password alone does not get you in.

If you lose your phone but still have a recovery code, type it in **Code** to sign in. Then set two-factor sign-in up again on the new phone.

Setting it up again, for example on another phone, replaces the key and the recovery codes and signs you out everywhere else. This browser stays signed in.

#### Signing in with a code

After your password, the page **Two-factor sign-in** says `Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.` Type the code in **Code** and press **Continue**. Spaces or hyphens inside the digits do not matter. A recovery code works once, and its letters may be in either case, with or without hyphens or spaces. **Start again** goes back to the password. A half-finished sign-in is dropped after the time your administrator allows, 10 minutes unless they have changed it.

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `The code is not correct.` | Type the code the app currently shows. A code works once, so if you sign in again straight away, wait for the app's next code. The same message appears on the set-up page when the first code is wrong, and the page shows the same key again. A used recovery code does not work again. Wrong codes count like wrong passwords. |
| `The password or the code is not correct.` | On the page **Two-factor sign-in** that asks for your password, check both and try again. |
| `Too many attempts. Try again in N seconds.` | Wait as long as the message says. |
| `The gateway cannot record changes right now, so it cannot accept a recovery code. Sign in with the code from your authenticator app, or try again later.` | Use the code from the app, or wait. |

### What you can see and do

The gateway shows you only what an administrator granted you. Each grant names brokers, Message VPNs and queues, and gives one of two levels.

| Level | What it lets you do on a queue |
| --- | --- |
| Operate | Browse the queue, forward messages and delete them. |
| Read-only | Browse the queue and forward messages. Queue Browser marks the queue with a **Read-Only** badge and hides **Delete**. Queue Copy can copy from it, but not move from it. |

- The **Broker** and **Message VPN** lists, and the queue lists in the pages, hold only what you were granted.
- If you type the name of a queue you were not granted, it does not bind, and Queue Browser says `You are not entitled to browse queue "orders.private".`
- In Queue Copy, the queue lists of the destination hold only queues on which you hold Operate, because copying into a queue changes it.
- The page applies the queue limits itself: the gateway checks that you were granted the broker, and the page then narrows each list to the queues you were granted.
- Queue Subscriptions lists only subscriptions on queues you may see, as the Queue Subscriptions chapter says.
- Queue Copy does not copy to a topic: it says `Topic destinations are unavailable with provisioned connections -- entitlements are defined per queue.` A destination queue you may not write to gives `You are not entitled to write to queue "orders.archive".`
- The sidebar shows Connections and About, and then only the pages your administrator gave you, out of Queue Browser, Queue Copy and Queue Subscriptions. A page you were not given is not listed. A change shows after you press **Refresh** or reload the page.

If an administrator takes away something you were using while you work, whatever depended on it stops. The gateway also closes your messaging connection when you sign out, in this tab or another, when your password or administrator status changes, and when an administrator removes your access to that broker or Message VPN. SEMP is closed with it, as in "The connected view" above.

### Other messages

| Message | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | The gateway ended your sign-in. Press **Sign in**. |
| `You must change your password before you continue.` | Press **Change password** and choose a password. |
| `Sign-in failed. Check the username and password.` | On the gateway's page: check both. The message is the same whatever went wrong. |
| `Sign-in could not be checked. Try again.` | The gateway could not look up your account. Try again. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` or, on the gateway's page, `Too many requests from this address. Wait a minute and try again.` | Wait a minute. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` | Check your network, then press **Refresh**. |
| `The gateway did not answer in time.` followed by a sentence about changes | If you were changing something, reload the page to see where things stand before you try again. |
| `Broker "east-prod" is not provisioned for this account.` or `VPN "default" is not provisioned on broker "east-prod".` | Your account does not hold that grant. Press **Refresh**, or ask your administrator. |
| `The broker refused the credential the gateway holds for it. Ask an administrator to check the connection.` | Only an administrator can fix this. |
| `The gateway could not reach the broker, or the broker gave an answer it cannot pass on. Its log has the cause.` | Tell your administrator. |
| `The gateway relays SEMP reads only; this request would change the broker.` | A Provisioned connection only reads through SEMP. Nothing is changed. |

---

## Administration

The administration app is where an administrator looks after a Provisioned gateway: its users, the brokers they reach, the gateway's settings, its certificates and its backups. This chapter covers who may open it, how to sign in, how to find your way around, and what every administration page has in common.

The administration app needs an administrator's session on the gateway. The gateway gives it to administrators only, and it never connects to a broker. Without a session, each page shows a gate in place of its content, and the first page, **Administration**, shows **Not signed in**.

What an operator sets up outside these pages, such as the environment variables, the first administrator account and recovery, is in the [Provisioned mode guide](provisioned-mode.md#administer).

### Who may open it

The administration app is a separate app from the one people use to browse queues. It lives at `/solAdmin` on the gateway, for example `https://your-gateway/solAdmin`.

- It exists only on a gateway that runs in Provisioned mode. On any other gateway, and at a wrong address, the gateway answers that the page is not found.
- Only an account marked as an administrator may open it. Any other account that signs in sees the gateway's **Administrator access required** page, which says `You are signed in as bob, which is not an administrator.` and offers **Back to the app**.
- The address with a trailing slash, `/solAdmin/`, takes you to `/solAdmin`.
- The gateway checks the administrator flag again on every request, so a change to your account applies at once.

### The page at a glance

![The Administration page of a visitor without a session: the sidebar lists the seven pages, and the page holds a Not signed in card with a message and a Sign in button.](../src/modules/admin-login/help/signed-out.svg)

*Figure 1. The Administration page while no one is signed in.*

1. The sidebar. Without a session it lists every page, starting with **Administration**. Each page other than **Administration** and **About** shows a gate until an administrator signs in.
2. The heading, **Not signed in**.
3. The reason, when the gateway gave one. With no session at all there is no message.
4. The button that takes you to the gateway's sign-in page. It reads **Sign in**, or **Change password** when the gateway says the password must be changed first.

This page is the signed-out screen and nothing more. While an administrator is signed in, it is hidden and the sidebar starts at **User Mgmt.**. It comes back when you sign out.

The message under the heading is one of these:

| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `You must change your password before you continue.` | The account has to set a new password first. The button reads **Change password** and leads to the gateway's password page. |
| `This account is not an administrator.` | You hold a session, but the account is not an administrator. Ask an administrator to give it that role, or use an administrator's account. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` | The browser could not contact the gateway. Check the address and your network, then reload the page. |
| `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | The gateway took too long to answer. Reload the page. |
| `The gateway sent a response this page cannot read.` | Something between you and the gateway, such as a proxy, answered in place of it. Ask whoever runs the gateway. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway limits how often one address may ask. Wait, then reload. |

Any other refusal shows the message under Other messages below, or `Unexpected answer from the gateway (HTTP 500).` with the status number it answered.

### Signing in

Sign-in does not happen inside the administration app. It happens on the gateway's own sign-in page, the same page the main app uses, and the gateway brings you back to `/solAdmin` when you are done.

1. Open `/solAdmin` on your gateway. With no session, the gateway sends you to its sign-in page. You can also press **Sign in** on the **Not signed in** card.
2. Type your username and password.
3. Press **Sign in**.
4. The gateway returns you to the administration app, which opens on **User Mgmt.**. If your account asks for them, the next two sections come first.

![The gateway's sign-in page: a dark header with the product name, then a Username box, a Password box and a Sign in button.](../src/modules/admin-login/help/sign-in.svg)

*Figure 2. The gateway's sign-in page.*

1. **Username**: up to 64 characters.
2. **Password**: shown as dots, up to 128 characters.
3. **Sign in** sends both to the gateway.

A refused sign-in shows a red message above the fields, or a page of its own:

| Message | Meaning and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Sign-in failed. Check the username and password.` | One of the two is wrong. The gateway does not say which. |
| `Too many attempts. Try again in 30 seconds.` | Too many wrong answers in a row, for this account or from this address. The number of seconds is the wait that applies, and it grows with each further failure. Wait, then try again. |
| **Sign-in unavailable**: `Sign-in could not be checked. Try again.` | The gateway could not read its user list. Try again, and tell whoever runs the gateway if it persists. |
| **Too many requests**: `Too many requests from this address. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway limits how many sign-in requests one address may make. Wait a minute. |
| **Request refused**: `This form was submitted from another site.` or `The form could not be read.` | The sign-in form came from somewhere other than the gateway. Open `/solAdmin` again and sign in from the gateway's own page. |

> [!TIP]
> The pages that show a message instead of a form offer **Back to the app**. It leads to the main app, not to the administration app. Type `/solAdmin` again to return.

#### A password that must be changed first

The gateway can require a new password before it lets an account do anything else. After a correct sign-in it then shows **Change password** with the line `You must set a new password before you continue.` and no way to skip it. Opening `/solAdmin` with such an account leads here too.

| Field | What it is | What it accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Current password** | The password you signed in with. | Up to 128 characters. |
| **New password** | The password to use at your next sign-in. | At least 12 characters unless the gateway's settings ask for more, and at most 128. The page prints the exact range under the fields, for example `12 to 128 characters.` |
| **Confirm new password** | The same password again. | The same range, and it must match. |

Press **Change password**. The gateway then returns you to the administration app. A password you change on your own initiative, from the sidebar (see Finding your way around below), shows the same page with a **Cancel** link that takes you back unchanged.

A refused change shows one of these:

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `The current password is not correct.` | Retype it. A wrong current password counts as a failed sign-in, with the same waits. |
| `The new passwords do not match.` | Type the same password in both boxes. |
| `The new password must be 12 to 128 characters.` | Choose a password inside the range the message names. |
| `The new password must differ from the current one.` | Choose a different password. |
| `The password could not be saved.` or `The password could not be checked. Try again.` | The gateway could not complete the change. Try again. |
| **Password not changed**: `Your account was changed while this request ran. Sign in again.` | Someone changed your account at the same moment. Sign in again and repeat the change. |
| **Password not changed**: `The gateway cannot record changes right now, so it refused this one. Try again later or tell an administrator.` | The gateway is set to refuse changes while its audit log cannot be written. |
| **Password not changed**: `The gateway's user file was changed outside the gateway. An administrator must restart the gateway before passwords can be changed.` | An administrator must restart the gateway from Gateway Settings or on its host. |

A password change ends your other sessions. The browser you changed it in stays signed in.

#### Two-factor sign-in

Two-factor sign-in asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app after the password. Whether you must use it depends on a setting that an administrator chooses in Gateway Settings. The [Provisioned mode guide](provisioned-mode.md#two-factor-sign-in) explains the choices.

When your account has it, the gateway shows **Two-factor sign-in** after a correct password:

1. Read `Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.`
2. Type the code in the **Code** box. A recovery code goes in the same box. Spaces and hyphens in a six-digit code are ignored.
3. Press **Continue**. The sign-in is complete once the code passes.

A wrong code shows `The code is not correct.` and counts as a failed sign-in. **Start again** returns to the password step. A sign-in that waits too long for its code is dropped, and you start again.

When the gateway requires two-factor and your account has none yet, the sign-in continues on **Set up two-factor sign-in**:

1. Scan the picture with an authenticator app, or type the key shown under it into the app.
2. Type the six digits the app shows in the **Code** box. Spaces and hyphens in a code are ignored.
3. Press **Turn on two-factor sign-in**.
4. The **Recovery codes** page lists the codes. Copy them somewhere safe, away from your phone: each works once, and they are shown only on this page. Press **Continue**.

You can set it up, or set it up again, at any time from the sidebar (see below). The gateway first asks you to confirm it is you, with your **Password** and, when two-factor is already on, your **Current code or a recovery code**. The page then offers **Continue** and a **Cancel** link, and a wrong answer shows `The password or the code is not correct.` Setting it up again replaces the authenticator and its recovery codes, and signs you out everywhere else.

> [!WARNING]
> A reset of two-factor sign-in is made from User Mgmt, and the account then sets it up again. If you lose both your phone and your recovery codes, you cannot sign in, so another administrator must reset it for you. The Provisioned mode guide covers [a lost phone](provisioned-mode.md#a-lost-phone), including the case of a lone administrator.

If the gateway is set to refuse changes while its audit log cannot be written, a recovery code cannot be used and the page says so. A code from the authenticator app still works.

### Finding your way around

Once you are signed in, the gateway's pages are in the sidebar, under your account.

![The administration app signed in as admin: the sidebar starts with three icons and the signed-in name, lists six pages, and User Mgmt. is open with Refresh, Add user, a search box and a table of users.](../src/modules/admin-login/help/signed-in.svg)

*Figure 3. The administration app signed in, on User Mgmt.*

1. The key icon, **Change password**.
2. The lock icon, **Two-factor sign-in**.
3. The arrow leaving a frame, **Sign out**.
4. Who is signed in: your username, with a small **admin** tag. Hold the pointer over the name to read `Signed in as admin`.
5. The pages of the app. The open page is highlighted.
6. The search box above a list (see Searching a list below).

#### The account block

The three icons and your name stay at the top of the sidebar on every page.

- **Change password** opens the gateway's password page, described above, and returns you to the administration app.
- **Two-factor sign-in** opens the gateway's page for setting two-factor up, or setting it up again, and returns you here.
- **Sign out** ends your session on the gateway and returns you to **Not signed in**. It asks no question.

When the sidebar is collapsed, the name is hidden and the icons stack one above the other.

#### The pages

| Sidebar entry | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| **User Mgmt.** | The people who sign in: their passwords, roles, the modules they may open and the queues they may reach. |
| **Conn. Mgmt** | The brokers the gateway reaches for its users, with their Message VPNs and credentials. |
| **Gateway Settings** | The gateway's own settings, and the button that restarts it. |
| **Certificates** | The gateway's certificate and the broker certificate authorities it trusts. |
| **Backup & Restore** | Saving the gateway's configuration to an encrypted backup, scheduling backups, and restoring one. |
| **About** | The app's version, and this manual in its Help tab. |

Each of these has its own chapter in this manual.

#### The gates

While no administrator is signed in, each page shows a gate with the heading **Administrator Sign-in Required** and a line that names the page's job. It means the same everywhere: sign in as an administrator.

| Page | The line under the heading |
| --- | --- |
| **User Mgmt.** | `Sign in as an administrator to manage users.` |
| **Conn. Mgmt** | `Sign in as an administrator to manage connections.` |
| **Gateway Settings** | `Sign in as an administrator to change the gateway settings.` |
| **Certificates** | `Sign in as an administrator to see or change the gateway's certificates.` |
| **Backup & Restore** | `Sign in as an administrator to back up or restore the gateway configuration.` |

### When your session ends

A session ends in these ways:

- You press **Sign out**.
- The gateway ends it. A session ends after it has been idle for a set time, and after a set total time whatever you do. The defaults are 10 and 30 minutes, and Gateway Settings changes them. A gateway restart ends every session. See [Sessions and sign-in](provisioned-mode.md#sessions-and-sign-in) in the Provisioned mode guide.
- Your account changes. Changing your password, setting two-factor up again, or an administrator's reset ends your other sessions.

The page does not poll the gateway. It notices when you next do something that needs the gateway, such as pressing **Refresh** or saving. A toast then says `Your session has ended. Sign in again.`, stays up for five seconds, and the app returns to **Not signed in**. A password typed into the user form is cleared. Press **Sign in**, and the gateway brings you back to the administration app.

Some changes to your own account end your session on purpose. Each shows a toast that says so, and returns you to **Not signed in**:

- Saving your own account with a password, or with the administrator flag changed: `Password changed. Sign in again.` or `Administrator flag changed. Sign in again.`
- Deleting your own account, after the question `Delete your own account "admin"? You will be signed out.`: `Account deleted. You have been signed out.`
- Resetting your own two-factor sign-in: `Two-factor sign-in reset. You have been signed out.`

#### When your administrator rights are taken away

The gateway reads the administrator flag on every request. If another administrator takes it from your account, your next action in a page is refused with `This needs an administrator.`, shown where that page shows its errors. Reload the page in your browser: the gateway then answers **Administrator access required**, as for any account that is not an administrator. If your account is deleted instead, opening `/solAdmin` again ends the session and sends you to the gateway's sign-in page.

The gateway also refuses to remove the last administrator: `At least one administrator must remain.`

### Things every page shares

#### Searching a list

The lists on **User Mgmt.** (by username) and **Conn. Mgmt** (by broker name or hostname) have a search box above the table. Its hint reads `Search users (* = any)` or `Search connections (* = any)`.

- The list narrows as you type. Nothing is sent to the gateway.
- Your text may match anywhere in the name, in any letter case.
- `*` stands for any run of characters. `ops*prod` finds `ops-eu-prod` but not `prod-ops`.
- With no match the table says `No users match "zed".` or `No connections match "zed".` With nothing loaded it says `No users.` or `No connections.`
- The text stays in the box when you press **Refresh**, so you see the fresh list narrowed the same way.

The search only narrows what you see. It is not the stricter matching of the rows that grant access to queues, which is anchored and respects letter case.

#### Row buttons and rows of boxes

Each row of a list ends in small buttons. Hold the pointer over one to read its name, for example `Edit user "alice"` or `Delete user "alice"`. A user whose two-factor sign-in is on also has a `Reset two-factor for user "alice"` button.

Where a form takes a list, such as the entitlements of a user or the Message VPNs of a connection, it shows a row of boxes for each entry, headed by the column names, with an add button below. A list with no rows shows a short note saying what that means. The cross at the end of a row, whose hint is `Remove row`, deletes that row from the form. A row whose boxes are all empty is ignored when you save. Nothing is saved until you save the form.

#### Confirm dialogs

Before something that is hard to undo, the app asks a question in a small window and waits. Its two buttons are **Cancel** and a button named for the action, such as **Delete**, **Reset** or **Reload**. Examples are `Delete user "bob"?` and `Reset two-factor sign-in for "bob"? They will have to set it up again.`

- **Cancel**, the <kbd>Esc</kbd> key and a click outside the window all answer no, and nothing happens.
- The action button has the focus when the window opens, so pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd> answers yes. Read the question first.

#### Saving at the same time as another administrator

Each user, each connection, the gateway settings and the backup schedule carry a version that the page reads with them and sends back with your save. The first save wins. If someone else saved the same thing after you opened it, your save is refused, not merged, and the page asks:

![A dialog saying that the user was changed by someone else since you opened it, with a Cancel button and a Reload button.](../src/modules/admin-login/help/conflict.svg)

*Figure 4. The dialog shown when another administrator saved first.*

1. The message. It begins `This user`, `This connection`, `This settings page` or `This schedule`, and continues `was changed by someone else since you opened it.`
2. **Cancel** keeps your form and what you typed, so you can copy it first.
3. **Reload** loads the current values. For a user or a connection it returns to the list and closes the form. For the settings and the schedule it refills the form. Redo your edit on top of theirs.

The same dialog appears when you press **Delete** on a row that changed after the list loaded. The unit is the whole record, so two administrators who edit different fields of one user still meet this dialog. Two administrators who edit different records never do.

If the other administrator deleted the record instead, a toast says `This user was deleted by someone else.` (or `This connection ...`) and the list reloads without it. Adding a name that exists already says `User "carol" already exists. Use Edit to change it.` or `Connection "east-prod" already exists. Use Edit to change it.`, whoever added it and when.

An import in **Backup & Restore** is checked the same way. It refuses with `The gateway's data changed since the preview. Run the preview again.` when a section it would replace changed after the preview. The [Provisioned mode guide](provisioned-mode.md#two-administrators-at-once) has the details.

#### Messages about the gateway's files

The gateway keeps the users, the connections, the backup schedule and its settings in files on its host, and its certificate and trust files in another folder. These messages mean the gateway could not use one. An administrator cannot cure the cause from these pages: tell whoever runs the gateway. The gateway's log has the details in every case.

| Message | Meaning and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `A data file (users, connections or backup settings) was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | A data file was changed outside the pages. Nothing for those files can be saved until the gateway restarts. |
| `config.yaml was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | The same for the settings file. Gateway Settings shows it as a banner and blocks saving until the restart. |
| `The gateway could not write its data files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The write failed, for example on a full disk, and was rolled back. Try again once the cause is fixed. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | The choice **Refuse changes until it can be written** is set in Gateway Settings and the audit log is failing. Changes wait until it can be written. |
| `The gateway cannot read its config.yaml. Its log has the cause.` | The settings file cannot be read. Nothing can be saved to it. |
| `The gateway's certificate or trust files are read-only on its host, so they cannot be changed here.` | The host forbids writing them. Retrying does not help until whoever runs the gateway makes them writable. |
| `The gateway could not write its certificate or trust files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The write failed and was rolled back, so the old certificate and authorities still stand. |
| `The gateway could not write the backup. Its log has the cause.` | A backup could not be saved. |
| `The gateway could not complete the request. Its log has the cause.` | An error the gateway did not expect. Try again, then ask whoever runs the gateway. |

#### Other messages

These refusals can appear on any page, as a toast or under the form you were saving:

| Message | Meaning and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | See When your session ends. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | Your account is not an administrator, or has lost the administrator flag. See above. |
| `You must change your password before you continue.` | Press **Change password** on **Not signed in**, and change it. |
| `Not found. It may already have been removed.` | The record is gone. Reload the page. |
| `This was changed by someone else since you opened it. Reload to see the current version.` | The record changed. Reload the page and repeat your edit. |
| `That name already exists. Use Edit to change it.` | Open the existing entry instead of adding it again. |
| `This change would lock this browser out of the gateway.` | The gateway refused a setting that would shut you out. It usually names the setting and the reason. |
| `The gateway refused a cross-site request.` | The request did not come from the gateway's own page. Reload the page from the gateway's address. |
| `The request is too large.` or `The gateway rejected the request as malformed.` | The gateway could not accept what the page sent. Reload and try again. |
| `The page did not send the version it was working from, so the gateway refused the change. Reload the page and try again.` | Reload the page. |

The [Troubleshooting](provisioned-mode.md#troubleshooting) section of the Provisioned mode guide covers the operator's side of these refusals.

---

## User Mgmt.

Decide who may sign in to the gateway, which brokers, Message VPNs and queues each person may reach, and which pages of the app they may open. You also reset two-factor sign-in here, and test what a saved user gets.

User Mgmt. is a page of the administration app, which the gateway serves at `/solAdmin` to administrators only. It needs an administrator's session. Without one, the page shows **Administrator Sign-in Required** and the line `Sign in as an administrator to manage users.` in place of everything below. How the gateway is set up, and how an operator prepares the settings these pages rely on, is in the [operator's guide](provisioned-mode.md#administer).

### The page at a glance

The page has two views. The list view shows every user, with the **Permission test** card under it. **Add user** and the edit button of a row replace both with the user form: three cards (the account, **Modules** and **Entitlements**) and the **Save** and **Cancel** buttons.

![The user list: Refresh and Add user buttons, a search box, and a table of three users with Username, Role and Two-factor columns and the row buttons.](../src/modules/user-management/help/list.svg)

*Figure 1. The user list, with one user who has two-factor sign-in turned on.*

1. **Refresh** loads the list from the gateway again. **Add user** opens the empty user form.
2. The search box. It narrows the list as you type.
3. The columns: **Username**, **Role** (`Admin` or `User`) and **Two-factor** (`On` or `Off`), then **Actions**.
4. The row buttons: **Reset two-factor** (the shield, only on a row where two-factor is `On`), **Edit** (the pencil) and **Delete** (the bin). Hover over a button to see its name, for example `Edit user "alice"`.

### Finding a user

Type in the search box, which reads `Search users (* = any)`. The list shows the users whose username contains your text, in any letter case. Put `*` in the text to stand for any run of characters: `a*e` finds `alice`. The search looks at usernames only, and it works on the list already loaded, so it never contacts the gateway.

An empty list says `No users.` A search that finds nothing says `No users match "text".`, with your text between the quotes. If the gateway cannot give the list, a red line under the table says why. Press **Refresh** to load the list again, for example after another administrator made a change.

### Adding a user

1. Press **Add user**. The form opens under the title **Add user**.
2. Type the **Username** and the **Password**. The rules are in the table below.
3. Switch on **Administrator** only if this person is to manage the gateway.
4. In **Modules**, leave **Deployment default** selected, or choose the modules for this user (see below).
5. In **Entitlements**, add the rows that give the user their brokers, Message VPNs and queues (see below).
6. Press **Save**. The toast `User saved` appears and the list returns with the user in it. **Cancel** returns to the list and keeps nothing.

### The account card

![The user form for alice: the account card with username, password and Administrator switch, and the Modules card with its two-part button, two module pills and an Add module button.](../src/modules/user-management/help/form-account.svg)

*Figure 2. The first two cards of the user form, here editing alice with a list of modules of her own.*

1. **Username**. You type it when you add a user. When you edit a user, it is fixed.
2. **Password**, with a hint after its name: `(required)` when you add a user, `(leave blank to keep current)` when you edit one.
3. The **Administrator** switch.
4. The button for the user's modules, with two parts: **Deployment default** and **Choose for this user**. The pressed part is the choice, and the line under it names what the default gives.
5. The modules the user may open, each as a pill.
6. **+ Add module**, which lists the modules you can still add.

| Field | What it accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Username** | 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ @ -`, and not only dots. Spaces around it are removed. It cannot be changed once the user exists: to rename someone, add the name you want and delete the old one. | Empty |
| **Password** | 12 to 128 characters. The lower limit is the **Minimum password length** of Gateway Settings when that is higher than 12. The page sends the password over TLS and the gateway stores only a hash of it. It is never shown again. When you edit a user, leave the box empty to keep the stored password. | Empty |
| **Administrator** | A switch. It lets the user open `/solAdmin`. It gives no access to any broker by itself: an administrator needs entitlement rows like anybody else. | Off |

> [!TIP]
> The password box forgets what you typed when you press **Cancel**, save, sign out or lose your session. Nothing you typed there stays in the page.

### Editing a user

1. Press the pencil on the user's row. The form opens under the title `Edit user "alice"`, filled with what is saved.
2. Change what you need. Leave **Password** empty unless you are setting a password.
3. Press **Save**.

The page sends the whole user each time, so a save replaces the user's flag, modules and both lists of entitlements with what the form shows.

### Deleting a user

1. Press the bin on the user's row.
2. Read the question, `Delete user "bob"?`, and press **Delete**. **Cancel** keeps the user.

The toast `User deleted` appears and the list reloads. The user's sessions end at once.

### Modules

The **Modules** card sets which pages of the app a user may open: Queue Browser, Queue Copy and Queue Subscriptions. The Connections page and the About page are always shown. Which of the three the gateway offers at all, and what a user without a list of their own gets, are set in Gateway Settings ([What users may open](provisioned-mode.md#what-users-may-open)).

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Deployment default** | The user gets what Gateway Settings give everyone. The modules it gives are named in the line under the button (or `no modules`) and shown as pills without a remove button. This is the choice for a user you add. If the settings change, so does what this user gets. |
| **Choose for this user** | The user has a list of their own. It starts as what the default gives. Each module is a pill with a remove button, named for screen readers `Remove Queue Browser` and so on. **+ Add module** opens a menu of the offered modules that are not in the list yet; pick one to add it, and press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to close the menu. The button is disabled when nothing is left to add. An empty list reads `No modules.` |

A pill marked `not offered` is a module the gateway does not offer. It has no effect until Gateway Settings offer it, and you can remove it. The gateway never gives a user a module it does not offer.

When you press **Deployment default** again, the user's own list is dropped on save.

### Entitlements

The **Entitlements** card decides which brokers, Message VPNs and queues the user reaches. A user without a row reaches nothing.

![The Entitlements card: a notice, a list of operate rows and a list of read-only rows, each row with three boxes and a remove button, and the Save and Cancel buttons below.](../src/modules/user-management/help/form-entitlements.svg)

*Figure 3. The Entitlements card with two operate rows and one read-only row.*

1. The notice at the top of the card. It begins `These entitlements cover queues only.` and says that the broker's own ACL profile decides where messages may go.
2. **Operate entitlements (read + write)**, and its **+ Add** button, which adds an empty row.
3. A row: three boxes under the headings **Brokers**, **Message VPNs** and **Queues**. An empty box shows the hint `brokers (e.g. *)`, `msgVpns (e.g. *)` or `queues (e.g. *)`.
4. The remove button of a row. Its tooltip is `Remove row`.
5. **Read-only entitlements**, with its own **+ Add** button.
6. **Save** and **Cancel**.

Each box holds a name or a pattern. A row gives access when the broker, the Message VPN and the queue all match their box. A row whose three boxes are all empty is ignored on save. A box left empty matches no name, so type `*` where any name will do.

| List | What its rows give | When it is empty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Operate entitlements (read + write)** | On a matching queue: browse, forward and delete messages, and copy into the queue. | `None: this user changes no queue (no delete, no copy into one). Read-only rows still let them browse.` |
| **Read-only entitlements** | On a matching queue: browse and forward messages. No delete, and no copy into the queue. | `None. With no operate rows either, this user can sign in but reaches no broker.` |

A user reaches a broker's Message VPN when any row, operate or read-only, matches that broker and that Message VPN. They see the queues that the queue boxes of those rows match. Where a queue matches rows of both lists, the operate row wins. The gateway enforces the broker and the Message VPN. The queue boxes are applied by the app itself.

#### How the wildcard matches

A pattern must match the whole name. `*` stands for any run of characters, including none. Every other character stands for itself: there is no `?` and there are no character classes. Matching is case-sensitive, so `Orders.*` does not match `orders.incoming`.

| Pattern | Matches | Does not match |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `*` | Any name. | None. |
| `orders.*` | `orders.incoming`, `orders.` | `orders`, `Orders.incoming` |
| `*.dlq` | `orders.incoming.dlq` | `orders.dlq.old` |
| `east-*` | `east-prod` | `west-test` |
| `default` | `default` only. | `default2` |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Entitlements cover queues only. Sending and forwarding messages depend on the broker: the ACL profile of the Message VPN's client username decides where messages may go, whatever the rows say. Give the gateway's broker accounts the least access they need, through their client profile and ACL profile on the broker. See [What it does not enforce](provisioned-mode.md#what-it-does-not-enforce).

### Testing what a user gets

The **Permission test** card, under the list, shows what a saved user gets on one queue. Use it after a change, instead of asking the user to try.

![The Permission test card: four boxes for the user, the broker, the Message VPN and the queue, and below them a green Operate answer, the matching row and the modules.](../src/modules/user-management/help/permission-test.svg)

*Figure 4. The Permission test card, answering for alice on one queue.*

1. **User**: a list of the saved users, starting with `Select a user...`.
2. **Broker**: the broker's name as it is in Connection Management.
3. **Message VPN**.
4. **Queue**.
5. The answer, as a label and a sentence.
6. The row that gave the answer, and the modules the user may open.

1. Pick a user.
2. Type the broker, the Message VPN and the queue. Type full names: the test matches them exactly and in the same letter case, and `*` counts as a wildcard only inside the user's rows.
3. Read the answer. It updates as you type. Until all four are filled in, the card says `Pick a user and enter a broker, Message VPN and queue.`

| Answer | It says | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Operate** | Browse, forward and delete messages, and copy into this queue. | An operate row matches the broker, the Message VPN and the queue. |
| **Read-only** | Browse and forward messages; no delete, no copy into this queue. | No operate row matches, and a read-only row does. |
| **Queue hidden** | Reaches this Message VPN, but no row's queue pattern matches this queue. | A row matches the broker and the Message VPN, but none matches the queue. |
| **No access** | No row matches this broker and Message VPN. | The user does not reach this Message VPN. |

Under the answer, `Matching row:` names the row that gave it, as its three boxes, and `Modules:` lists the modules the user may open, or `none`. The test reads the user as saved, never the form you have open. It cannot see the broker's own queue permissions, which still apply, and the broker and Message VPN must be in Connection Management for anyone to reach them.

### Resetting two-factor sign-in

The **Two-factor** column says `On` when the user has set up a code from an authenticator app. Use the reset for a user who lost their phone and their recovery codes.

1. Press the shield on the user's row. The button exists only where the column says `On`. Its tooltip is `Reset two-factor for user "alice"`.
2. Read the question, `Reset two-factor sign-in for "alice"? They will have to set it up again.`, and press **Reset**.
3. The toast `Two-factor sign-in reset` appears and the list reloads. The column reads `Off`.

The reset ends the user's sessions. It leaves the password as it is. What the user must do at the next sign-in depends on the gateway's two-factor mode ([A lost phone](provisioned-mode.md#a-lost-phone)). A save of the user form never changes two-factor, in either direction.

### Forcing a password change

An account can be marked so that its owner may use only the password page until they change it. This page has no control for it and the list does not show it. The gateway marks the first administrator it creates, named `admin`, this way, and that person changes the password at the first sign-in ([Start it](provisioned-mode.md#start-it)). A password you save here clears the mark. To change only your own password, use **Change password** in the account control of the sidebar.

### What a change does to a user who is signed in

| You change | The user, signed in at that moment |
| --- | --- |
| The password, the **Administrator** switch, or you delete the user | All their sessions end and their open broker connections close. They sign in again, with the password you set if you changed it. |
| You reset two-factor | All their sessions end and their open broker connections close. They sign in again. |
| The entitlements | They stay signed in. The gateway applies the rows to their next request, and closes any broker connection to a Message VPN they may not reach. |

#### Your own account

The gateway lets you change your own account. When the change ends your session, the page asks the app to sign you out, so you sign in again.

- Setting a password for yourself: the toast `Password changed. Sign in again.`
- A change to your own **Administrator** switch: `Administrator flag changed. Sign in again.`
- Deleting yourself asks `Delete your own account "admin"? You will be signed out.` and ends with `Account deleted. You have been signed out.`
- Resetting your own two-factor asks `Reset your own two-factor sign-in? You will be signed out and must set it up again.` and ends with `Two-factor sign-in reset. You have been signed out.`
- Saving only your own entitlements or modules keeps you signed in and shows `User saved`.

### When the gateway refuses

A refusal on the form shows in red under **Save** and keeps what you typed. A refusal of a delete or a reset shows as a red toast. A refusal while loading the list shows under the table. A refusal that says your session has ended shows as a red toast on every page, and the app signs you out.

| Message | Why | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Username is required.` | The username box is empty. | Type a username. |
| `A password is required for a new user.` and `A new user needs a password.` | You add a user with an empty password. The page checks first and the gateway checks again. | Type a password. |
| `User "bob" already exists. Use Edit to change it.` | The username is taken. | Press **Cancel** and edit that user, or choose another name. |
| `Username must be 1 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ @ -, not only dots.` | The username breaks the rule in the table above. | Change the username. |
| `Password must be 12 to 128 characters.` | The password is too short or too long. The first number is the gateway's minimum, which may be higher than 12. | Type a password within the limits. |
| `At least one administrator must remain.` | You delete the only administrator, or clear the flag of the only administrator. | Make another user an administrator first. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | Your account is not an administrator's. | Sign in with an administrator account. |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | The gateway ended your session. | Sign in again. The page asks the app to sign you out. |
| `This user was changed by someone else since you opened it.` | Another administrator saved the same user first. A dialog shows the message with **Reload** and **Cancel**. | Press **Reload** to see the current user, then repeat your change. **Cancel** keeps your form open. See [Two administrators at once](provisioned-mode.md#two-administrators-at-once). |
| `This user was deleted by someone else.` | The user is gone. A red toast shows the message and the page returns to the reloaded list. | Nothing: the user no longer exists. |
| `The gateway could not write its data files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway could not store the change. | Ask the operator to read the gateway's log. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway is set to refuse changes while it cannot record them. | Ask the operator to read the gateway's log. |
| `A data file (users, connections or backup settings) was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | The users file changed outside the gateway. | Ask the operator to restart the gateway. |
| `The gateway could not complete the request. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway failed in a way it did not expect. | Ask the operator to read the gateway's log. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway limits how fast requests may come. | Wait, then try again. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` and `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | The gateway did not answer. | Press **Refresh** and check the user before you try again. |

> [!WARNING]
> Deleting a user, and a reset of two-factor sign-in, cannot be undone from this page. A deleted user must be added again, with a password and entitlement rows.

---

## Conn. Mgmt

Keep the list of brokers the gateway reaches for its users. For each broker you set where it is, the account the gateway uses to manage it, and the Message VPNs with the credentials users connect with.

Conn. Mgmt is a page of the administration app at `/solAdmin`, and it needs a signed-in administrator. In any other session, signed out or signed in as a user who is not an administrator, the page shows **Administrator Sign-in Required** and the line `Sign in as an administrator to manage connections.` in place of everything below. Sign in as an administrator and the page loads the list by itself.

Users never see these details. They pick a broker and a Message VPN by name, and the gateway uses the stored account and credentials on their behalf. The setup of the gateway itself is in [the operator's guide](provisioned-mode.md#administer).

### The page at a glance

The page has two views: the list of connections, and the form you use to add or edit one. Figure 1 shows the list.

![The Conn. Mgmt list: Refresh and Add connection buttons, a search box, and a table of brokers with their hosts and an edit and a delete button on each row.](../src/modules/connection-management/help/list.svg)

*Figure 1. The list of connections, with two brokers.*

1. **Refresh** loads the list from the gateway again.
2. **Add connection** opens the form for a broker that is not in the list.
3. The search box. Its hint reads `Search connections (* = any)`.
4. One row for each connection: its **Broker** name and its **Host**. An appliance's row gives its management hostname, then its messaging hostname in brackets.
5. The **Actions** of the row: the pencil edits the connection, the bin deletes it.

### Finding a connection

Type in the search box and the list narrows as you type. A row stays when your text appears in its broker name or in what its **Host** column shows, in any letter case: `east` finds `East-Prod` and `east.example.com`. Put `*` in the text to stand for any run of characters: `e*prod` finds `east-prod`. Changing the text never contacts the gateway.

With no connections, the table says `No connections.` When the search matches none, it says `No connections match "your text".` If the list cannot be loaded, the reason shows in red under the table.

Press **Refresh** to load the list again, for example after another administrator made a change. It also takes you back to the list if the form is open.

### Adding a connection

1. Press **Add connection**. The form opens with the title **Add connection**, `https` and `wss` chosen as the schemes, and no ports or Message VPNs.
2. Fill in the broker's name and choose its type, then fill in the **SEMP (management)** and **Client (messaging)** parts, each with its hostname. Figure 2 and the tables below say what each field takes.
3. Under **Message VPNs (name / user / password)**, press **+ Add** once for each Message VPN users may connect to, and fill in its row.
4. Press **Save**. The page shows the toast `Connection saved` and returns to the list, loaded again.

The form is the same one you use to edit a connection, so Figure 2 shows it with a connection open.

![The connection form open on east-prod: broker name and broker type, the SEMP part with its scheme, hostname and port on one row and the account below, the Client part with its scheme, messaging hostname and port on one row, two Message VPN rows, Save and Cancel, and a red message under the form.](../src/modules/connection-management/help/form.svg)

*Figure 2. The form, editing the connection east-prod.*

1. **Broker name**: the name users and the gateway call this broker by.
2. **Solace Event Broker Type**: **Software / Cloud** for a broker with one hostname, **Appliance** for one with two.
3. The SEMP address on one row, read as a URL: **Scheme**, **Hostname** (where the broker is) and **Port**.
4. The SEMP **Username**.
5. The SEMP **Password**. While you edit, its hint reads `(leave blank to keep current)`.
6. The messaging address on one row: **Scheme**, **Messaging hostname** and **Port**. The hostname is locked for a software or cloud broker, where it shows the hostname above.
7. **+ Add** adds a row to the Message VPN list.
8. One row for each Message VPN: its name, the client username and the client password. The cross at the end of a row removes it.
9. **Save** stores the connection. **Cancel** returns to the list and keeps nothing.
10. The place where the form tells you what is wrong.

### The fields of the form

#### The broker

| Field | What it is | What it accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Broker name** | The name of the connection. Users are granted brokers by this name, and the list is kept by it. | Required. 1 to 64 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`, and not only dots. The name must not be in the list already. While you edit, the box is locked: the name is what identifies the connection. |
| **Solace Event Broker Type** | How many addresses the broker has. A software or cloud broker answers SEMP and messaging on one hostname. A Solace appliance answers SEMP on its management address and messaging on another. | **Software / Cloud** or **Appliance**. The form opens a connection that has one hostname as **Software / Cloud**, and one that has two as **Appliance**. |
| **Hostname** | The middle box of the first row under **SEMP (management)**. The address the gateway connects to: for both SEMP and messaging on a software or cloud broker, and for SEMP on an appliance, where its label reads **Management hostname**. | Required. A bare host name (`A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`, up to 253 characters, beginning and ending with a letter, a digit or `_`) or an IP address. IPv6 goes without brackets. No `https://`, no port, no path, no spaces. |
| **Messaging hostname** | The middle box of the row under **Client (messaging)**. For **Software / Cloud** it is locked and shows the hostname. For **Appliance** it is the address the gateway connects to for messaging. | Required for an appliance, by the rules of **Hostname**. It starts with the hostname already typed. The same hostname in both boxes is stored as one, and the connection opens again as **Software / Cloud**. |

#### SEMP (management)

SEMP is how the gateway reads a broker's configuration for its users: queues, subscriptions and the like. The gateway signs in with the account you give here and passes on to each user only what that user is granted.

| Field | What it accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheme** | `https (TLS)` or `http (plain)`. Choose `http` only for a broker whose SEMP port does not serve TLS, on a network you trust: the gateway then reaches it unencrypted, and the account's password crosses that hop in clear text. | `https (TLS)` |
| **Port** | A whole number from 1 to 65535, in digits only. A blank port is never taken to mean a default. Required when a SEMP username is set. A connection with no SEMP port gives users no management access to the broker. | Blank |
| **Username** | Up to 32 characters from `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`. It may be left blank. | Blank |
| **Password** | The account's password, typed with its characters hidden. The gateway refuses control characters in it and applies no other rule of its own. | Blank |

> [!TIP]
> Give the gateway a read-only or least-privilege SEMP account. It needs no more than users are meant to see.

#### Client (messaging)

Messaging is how a user's browser connects to the broker, through the gateway, to browse and copy messages.

| Field | What it accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Scheme** | `wss (TLS)` or `ws (plain)`. Choose `ws` only for a broker that does not serve TLS on its messaging port, on a network you trust: the credentials of the Message VPNs then cross that hop in clear text. | `wss (TLS)` |
| **Port** | As the SEMP port: digits, 1 to 65535. Required once a Message VPN is listed. | Blank |

The two schemes are chosen separately. A connection stored with no scheme shows `https` and `wss`.

#### Message VPNs

A user connects to one Message VPN of a broker, with the client username and password you store for it. The list of Message VPNs tells the gateway which VPNs exist on the broker and which credential opens each. While the list is empty the form says `None: no user can reach this broker until it lists a Message VPN.`

| Column | What it accepts |
| --- | --- |
| **Message VPN** | The VPN's name on the broker. Required for each row, and no two rows may carry the same name. Users are granted VPNs by this name. |
| **Client username** | Up to 189 printable ASCII characters (a space is allowed), without `?` or `*`. Letter case counts. A blank username passes the check. |
| **Client password** | The credential for that username, typed with its characters hidden. The gateway refuses control characters in it. While you edit, a blank box keeps the stored password. On a row you add, a blank box stores an empty password, for a client username that has none. The box's hint reads `password (blank = keep)`, and its other hints read `vpn name` and `username`. |

A row in which every box is empty is ignored when you save.

### Passwords

Passwords are sent to the gateway as you type them, over the connection to the gateway, and the gateway keeps them in its encrypted store. No page of the app shows a stored password again, and the list does not carry one. The boxes stay empty when you open a connection to edit it.

- To keep a password, leave its box blank. This holds for the SEMP password and for each Message VPN's password.
- To replace a password, type the replacement in its box.
- A stored VPN password belongs to the VPN's name. A row you add has none, and saves with an empty password if you leave its box blank.
- A row whose name you change has no stored password under its new name, so it needs one typed in. If you leave it blank, **Save** refuses and the form says `VPN "qa" has no stored password to keep. Enter its password, or save the removal of the other VPN first to add this one with none.` The form reads a stored name that has gone from the list as a change of name. So to remove one VPN and add another that has no password, save the removal first.
- What you typed is cleared when the form closes, by **Cancel**, by **Save**, or when your session ends.

### Editing a connection

1. In the list, press the pencil on the row. The form opens with the title `Edit connection "east-prod"` and the stored values, without passwords.
2. Change what you need. The broker name cannot be changed. To rename a connection, add it again under the other name, with all its passwords, and delete the old one.
3. Press **Save**. The page shows `Connection saved` and returns to the list.

Pressing **Cancel** returns to the list and drops your edits.

### Deleting a connection

1. In the list, press the bin on the row.
2. A question appears: `Delete connection "west-test"?` Press **Delete** to confirm, or **Cancel**, <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a click outside the question to keep the connection.
3. The page shows `Connection deleted` and loads the list again.

![Two questions the page asks: whether to delete the connection west-test, and whether to reload after someone else changed a connection.](../src/modules/connection-management/help/dialogs.svg)

*Figure 3. The question before a deletion, and the question when someone else changed the connection first.*

1. The question names the connection you are about to delete.
2. **Cancel** keeps it. **Delete** removes it for good.
3. The message when another administrator saved the same connection after you opened it.
4. **Reload** loads the list again and closes the form. **Cancel** keeps the form and your edits open.

> [!WARNING]
> A deleted connection cannot be brought back from this page, and its stored passwords go with it. To get it back you add it again, or import a backup.

### What a change does to users who are connected

A change applies at once. The gateway reads the stored connection every time it connects a user or relays a request, so no one has to sign in again.

- **Editing the address, ports, schemes or credentials.** Management requests and connections made from then on use the values you saved. A messaging connection that is already open stays open. If it drops, the browser connects again and gets the stored credential as it is then.
- **Removing a Message VPN from the list, or changing its name.** Users who are connected through that VPN are disconnected at once, because the VPN they use is not in the list under that name. A rename counts as a removal of the old name.
- **Deleting the connection.** Users connected through any of its VPNs are disconnected at once. Their requests for that broker are refused with `Not found. It may already have been removed.`
- **An empty VPN list.** No user can reach the broker, so every open connection to it closes.

The page has no button to test a connection. A connection that cannot be reached shows when a user tries to use it. A user whose request meets a wrong password sees `The broker refused the credential the gateway holds for it. Ask an administrator to check the connection.` A user whose request meets a wrong address, port or scheme sees `The gateway could not reach the broker, or the broker gave an answer it cannot pass on. Its log has the cause.`

Each save and each deletion is written to the gateway's audit trail with your name and the parts that changed, never a password. See [Audit trail](provisioned-mode.md#audit-trail).

### When the page or the gateway refuses

Before it sends a save, the page checks a few things and says what is wrong under the form. The message stays until you save again or leave the form.

| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Broker name is required.` | The **Broker name** box is empty. |
| `Connection "east-prod" already exists. Use Edit to change it.` | You are adding a name that is in the list. The gateway gives the same answer if the list on your screen is out of date and another administrator added the name meanwhile. |
| `Messaging hostname is required for an appliance. Choose Software / Cloud for a broker with one hostname.` | The type is **Appliance** and the **Messaging hostname** box is empty. |
| `VPN "qa" has no stored password to keep. Enter its password, or save the removal of the other VPN first to add this one with none.` | A VPN row has no password, the connection holds none for that name, and a stored VPN's name has gone from the list in the same save. Type the password. If the row is a VPN you are adding with no password, save the removal of the other VPN first. |
| `SEMP username may be up to 32 characters: letters, digits, - and _.` | The SEMP **Username** breaks its rule. |
| `VPN "qa": Client username must not exceed 189 characters.` | A client username is too long. |
| `VPN "qa": Client username may contain only printable ASCII characters: no accented letters or control characters.` | A client username holds a character outside the printable ASCII range. |
| `VPN "qa": Client username must not contain ? or *.` | The broker reads those two characters as wildcards, so they cannot be in a username. |

The gateway checks every save again, whatever the page let through, and gives the reason in its own words. The page shows it under the form, and nothing is stored. The reasons name the connection, and never print a password.

| The gateway says | What to change |
| --- | --- |
| `broker "east prod" must be 1 to 64 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -, not only dots` | The broker name. |
| `broker "east-prod": hostname "https://east.example.com" must be a host name (A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -) or an IP address, without scheme or port` | The hostname. The same message appears for an empty hostname. A messaging hostname the gateway refuses is named `client.hostname` in the same message. |
| `broker "east-prod": semp.port "abc" is not a port (1 to 65535)` | The SEMP port. The messaging port is named `client.port` in the same message. |
| `broker "east-prod": semp.port is required when a SEMP username is set` | Give the SEMP port, or clear the SEMP username. |
| `broker "east-prod": client.port is required when message VPNs are listed` | Give the messaging port, or remove the VPNs. |
| `broker "east-prod": a message VPN has no name` | A VPN row has a username or a password but no name. |
| `broker "east-prod": message VPN "default" appears more than once` | Two rows carry one name. Keep one. |
| `broker "east-prod": the SEMP username must be up to 32 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` | The SEMP username. |
| `broker "east-prod": message VPN "qa": the client username must be up to 189 printable ASCII characters, without ? or *` | The client username of that VPN. |
| `broker "east-prod": the SEMP username and password must not contain control characters, and the username no ':'` | Retype the SEMP username or password. |
| `broker "east-prod": message VPN "qa": the name, username and password must not contain control characters` | Retype the row. |

A connection that is already stored, or that came in from a restored backup, loads as it is even when a username breaks these rules. Saving it asks for a valid one.

These other answers can come back from a save, a deletion or loading the list. A save shows them under the form, a deletion in a toast, and loading the list in red under the table. The one exception is `Your session has ended. Sign in again.`, which always shows as a toast.

| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| The question `This connection was changed by someone else since you opened it.` with **Reload** | Another administrator saved or changed the same connection after you opened it. Your save or deletion is not applied. **Reload** shows the current values and you make your change again. See [Two administrators at once](provisioned-mode.md#two-administrators-at-once). |
| The toast `This connection was deleted by someone else.` | The connection is gone. The page loads the list again. |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | The gateway ended your session. The page asks you to sign out; sign in again to go on. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | The session you are using is not an administrator's. |
| `A data file (users, connections or backup settings) was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | Someone changed a file of the gateway outside these pages. Restart the gateway from Gateway Settings, and make the change again. |
| `The gateway could not write its data files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The save did not happen. Ask whoever runs the gateway to look at its log. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway is set to refuse every change while it cannot record it. |
| `The page did not send the version it was working from, so the gateway refused the change. Reload the page and try again.` | Reload the page in your browser, then make the change again. |
| `The gateway rejected the request as malformed.` | Make the change again. If it repeats, ask whoever runs the gateway to look at its log. |
| `The request is too large.` | The gateway refused the save as too large. Ask whoever runs the gateway to look at its log. |
| `The gateway refused a cross-site request.` | Use the page from the gateway's own address, `/solAdmin`. |
| `The gateway could not complete the request. Its log has the cause.` | The save did not happen. Ask whoever runs the gateway to look at its log. |
| `The gateway sent a response this page cannot read.` | Press **Refresh** and check the list before you repeat the change. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | Wait, then try again. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` | The browser got no answer. Check your network, then try again. |
| `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | Press **Refresh**, and check the list before you repeat the change. |

---

## Gateway Settings

Change how the gateway behaves: which connection tabs the app offers, who may reach it, how long sessions last, how sign-in is protected, which modules users may be given, and what is logged and audited. A saved setting applies at once.

Gateway Settings needs an **administrator's session**. Without one, the page shows **Administrator Sign-in Required** and the message `Sign in as an administrator to change the gateway settings.` in place of the settings. It is a page of the administration app, which the gateway serves at `/solAdmin` to administrators only.

What an operator sets up outside these pages, such as the environment variables the gateway starts with, is in the [Provisioned mode guide](provisioned-mode.md#configure).

### The page at a glance

The page is a stack of cards, one for each group of settings, with **Save** under them and a **Gateway** card at the foot. You change as many settings as you like, then press **Save** once.

![The Gateway Settings page: an intro card with Reload, a warning banner, the Connections and Access cards, a stack of further cards, and the Save button.](../src/modules/gateway-settings/help/page.svg)

*Figure 1. Gateway Settings, with the warning banner showing.*

1. The intro card and **Reload**. Reload fetches the settings from the gateway again and drops any change you have not saved.
2. The warning banner, shown only when the gateway's settings file was changed on the gateway host. See "When the settings file was changed on the host" below.
3. The **Connections** card.
4. The **Access** card.
5. The cards that follow, in this order: **Sessions**, **Sign-in throttle**, **Passwords and two-factor sign-in**, **Modules**, **Logging**, **Audit trail** and **Broker trust**.
6. **Save**. A refusal appears in red under it.

> [!NOTE]
> Every setting on this page applies at once, on Save. None of them waits for a restart. The gateway's certificate and the trusted broker CAs are not here: they are on the Certificates page.

### Reload and Save

When the page opens, it shows the settings the gateway holds at that moment. **Reload** shows them again.

1. Change the settings you need, in any cards.
2. Press **Save**. The button is off while the gateway checks and writes the settings.
3. The page says `Settings saved` and shows the values the gateway keeps, which can differ in small ways from what you typed. For example, the gateway drops blank lines from a list and orders the modules as the app does.

The gateway checks every value as it does at start. If any one is refused, none of the settings is saved, and the reason appears in red under **Save**. What the gateway refuses is listed under "What Save refuses" below.

### Connections

| Field | What it does | Choices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Connection modes the app offers** | Which connection tabs people see in the app. | **Provisioned only (everyone signs in)**: users sign in and use the brokers they were given. **Direct and Provisioned**: users may also type a broker's details into the Direct form. |
| **Tab shown first when both are offered** | The tab the app opens on when both are offered. | **Direct** (the default) or **Provisioned**. |

The page offers only these two modes, because this app is served only while the gateway runs in Provisioned mode. The gateway also refuses to save a setting that would turn Provisioned mode off, because that would turn this app off with it.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> With **Direct and Provisioned**, anyone who knows a broker's credentials can connect through the Direct form, outside the grants you give people. Offer it only where that is acceptable. The operator's side of this choice is in [Connection modes](provisioned-mode.md#connection-modes).

### Access

The Access card decides which computers may reach the gateway at all. It opens with one line that says which address the gateway takes your browser for. Read it before you change either list.

![Three cards of Gateway Settings: Access with the client address line and two address lists side by side, Modules with three toggle tiles and a select, and Audit trail with two switches and a select.](../src/modules/gateway-settings/help/cards.svg)

*Figure 2. The Access, Modules and Audit trail cards.*

1. The line that names your address and how the gateway worked it out.
2. **Allowed clients**, one range on each line, on the left.
3. **Trusted reverse proxies**, one range on each line, on the right.
4. The **Modules signed-in users may be given** tiles. A tile with a tick is offered.
5. **A user without a list of their own gets**.
6. **Copy audit lines to the gateway log (stdout)**.
7. **Also audit broker access**.
8. **If the audit log cannot be written**.

#### Your address as the gateway sees it

The line begins `Your address as the gateway sees it:` and then says one of these things.

| The line ends | It means |
| --- | --- |
| `(the TCP peer).`, followed by advice | The gateway took the address of the connection itself. If that is a proxy's or Docker's address and not yours, every user looks like it. For a reverse proxy, list it under **Trusted reverse proxies** and have it pass `X-Forwarded-For`. |
| `(from X-Forwarded-For, sent by the trusted proxy ...).` | The connection came from a proxy you listed, and the gateway believed the address that proxy passed on. |
| `unknown.` and where the connection comes from | The gateway could not read the `X-Forwarded-For` header. While the address is unknown, a non-empty **Allowed clients** list cannot be saved. |
| `unavailable.` | The page could not ask the gateway for your address. |

#### The two lists

| Field | What it does | What it accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Allowed clients: CIDR ranges, one per line (empty admits every client)** | Only clients whose address lies in one of these ranges may reach the gateway. Empty (the default) admits every client. | One range on each line, such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `192.0.2.7/32`. The slash and the prefix length are required, so a bare address is refused. Use the IPv4 form for an IPv4 address: an IPv6-mapped one such as `::ffff:10.0.0.1/128` is refused. Blank lines and spaces around a line are dropped. |
| **Trusted reverse proxies: CIDR ranges, one per line** | The proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For` header the gateway believes. Without one, it takes the connection's own address as the client. Empty by default. | The same form as above. |

> [!WARNING]
> An allow list shuts out every client outside it. The gateway refuses a list that would shut out the browser you are using, but it cannot know about anyone else. Check the ranges before you press **Save**.

### Sessions
