A session is a signed-in browser. These limits apply to every user, administrators included.

| Field | What it does | Accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Idle limit (minutes)** | A session ends after this long without a request. | A whole number from 1 up to the absolute limit. | 10 |
| **Absolute limit (minutes)** | A session ends this long after sign-in, however busy it is. | A whole number from 1 to 1440 (a day). | 30 |
| **Broker connects per user per minute** | How many broker credential requests and messaging sockets one user may open in a minute. | A whole number from 1 to 1000. | 20 |

The gateway also caps how many messaging sockets stay open at once: 20 for one user and 1000 for the whole gateway. Both are fixed and have no setting. A socket beyond either cap is refused until one closes. The connects per minute limit above bounds how fast sockets open, and these caps bound how many stay open.

### Sign-in throttle

The throttle slows down anyone who keeps getting a password or a code wrong. After a number of failures, the gateway makes the account, and the client address, wait before it checks another attempt. The wait starts at the first back-off and doubles with each further failure, up to the longest back-off. A successful sign-in clears the account's failures, but never the client's: those fade by themselves after the time you set.

| Field | What it does | Accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Count failures per client address** | A switch. On, the gateway counts failures for each client address as well as for each account, which catches guesses spread over many usernames. Off, it counts per account only. Turn it off only where every user reaches the gateway from one address: with it on, one person's typos would slow everyone down. | On or off. | On |
| **Failed sign-ins per account before a back-off** | How many failures one account may have before it must wait. | 1 to 1000. | 5 |
| **Failed sign-ins per client before a back-off** | How many failures one client address may have, across all accounts, before it must wait. Not used while the switch is off. | 1 to 1000. | 10 |
| **Forget failures after (minutes)** | A count is forgotten after this long without another failure. | 1 to 1440. | 15 |
| **First back-off (seconds)** | The first wait. | 1 up to the longest back-off. | 30 |
| **Longest back-off (seconds)** | The longest the wait can grow to. | 1 to 86400. | 900 |
| **Requests and sign-in attempts per minute per client** | How many requests without a session, and sign-in attempts, one client address may make in a minute. A script cannot try passwords faster than this, however failures are counted. Raise it if many users share one address. | 1 to 10000. | 60 |

The gateway counts an IPv6 client by its `/64` block, because one host usually owns a whole block.

### Passwords and two-factor sign-in

The card says: `A raised minimum length applies at the next password change; passwords already set keep working.`

| Field | What it does | Accepts | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimum password length** | The shortest password a user may set. It can only tighten the gateway's own rule, which is 12. | 12 to 128. | 12 |
| **Two-factor sign-in (code from an authenticator app)** | Who must give a code from an authenticator app as well as the password. It applies at the next sign-in, and it cannot be switched off. | See the next table. | Optional |
| **Time to finish two-factor after the password (minutes)** | How long a sign-in that has passed the password waits for its code. A shorter time also ends sign-ins that are already waiting. | 1 to 60. | 10 |

| Two-factor choice | Who signs in with a code |
| --- | --- |
| **Optional** | Those who have set it up. |
| **Administrators must use it** | Those who have set it up, and every administrator, who must set it up if they have not. |
| **Everyone must use it** | Everyone. |

A wrong code counts as a wrong password and brings the same waits. How people set two-factor sign-in up, and what to do when someone loses their phone, is in the [Two-factor sign-in](provisioned-mode.md#two-factor-sign-in) section of the Provisioned mode guide.

### Modules

This card decides which pages of the user app a signed-in user may open. The pages for signing in and the administration pages are not on offer here: the first is always shown, and the others belong to administrators.

| Field | What it does | Choices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Modules signed-in users may be given** | A row of toggle tiles, one for each module, each with its name and a line saying what it does. A tile with a tick is offered. Click a tile, or press <kbd>Space</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> on it, to switch it. A module that is not offered is out of reach for every user, whatever their own list says. | **Queue Browser**: Browse, inspect and delete queued messages. **Queue Copy**: Copy or move messages between queues. **Queue Subscriptions**: See which topics each queue subscribes to. All three are offered by default. |
| **A user without a list of their own gets** | What a user receives when no list has been set on their account. A user who has a list gets what it names, among the modules on offer. | **Every offered module** (the default) or **No modules**. |

A user's own list is set on the User Management page.

### Logging

| Field | What it does | Choices |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Log level** | How much the gateway writes to its own log: **debug** writes the most and **error** the least. | **debug**, **info**, **warn** (the default) and **error**. |

### Audit trail

The gateway always writes an audit trail of what administrators and users do, to `/data/audit.log` on the gateway. The settings on this card only add to it, and they apply from the next recorded event.

| Field | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Copy audit lines to the gateway log (stdout)** | Also writes each audit line to the gateway's own log, for a log shipper that reads it. | Off |
| **Also audit broker access: dials, SMF sockets and SEMP relay requests** | Adds a line each time a user is given broker credentials, opens a messaging socket or sends a request through the gateway to a broker. | Off |
| **If the audit log cannot be written** | What the gateway does when a line cannot be written, for example because the disk is full. **Carry on, and log the lost record** logs the loss and carries on. **Refuse changes until it can be written** also refuses every change until a line can be written again. | Carry on, and log the lost record |

> [!WARNING]
> With **Refuse changes until it can be written**, a full disk stops you changing users, connections, settings, certificates and backups. Reading, signing in as usual and **Restart gateway** still work. Choose it only if something watches the gateway's log and its disk. More is in the [Audit trail](provisioned-mode.md#audit-trail) section of the Provisioned mode guide.

### Broker trust

This card decides how the gateway checks the certificate of a broker it connects to. Both settings apply on Save, with no restart.

| Field | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Trust the standard root CAs** | The gateway trusts the public root CAs its image carries (Mozilla's list), as well as the CA files you add on the Certificates page. With the switch off, only the CA files are trusted. | On |
| **Skip broker certificate checks (insecure)** | The gateway connects to a broker without checking its certificate at all, so it cannot tell the broker from an impostor. | Off |

> [!WARNING]
> Leave **Skip broker certificate checks (insecure)** off outside a test. With it on, the gateway cannot tell a real broker from an impostor.

### What Save refuses

A refusal changes nothing: no setting is saved. The text appears in red under **Save**.

#### A number the page cannot read

A whole-number field that is empty, or holds anything but a whole number, stops the save before it is sent. The page says `<setting> must be a whole number.`, naming the setting by its key, for example `session.idleMinutes must be a whole number.`

#### A value the gateway refuses

The gateway checks every value as it does at start and answers with the setting and the allowed range, in this form: `key "session.absoluteMinutes" has invalid value "2000": must be 1 to 1440`. The ranges are those in the tables above. Two refusals carry a second figure:

- An idle limit above the absolute limit: `key "session.idleMinutes" has invalid value "40": must be 1 to 30 (session.absoluteMinutes is 30)`.
- A first back-off above the longest back-off: `key "login.backoffSeconds" has invalid value "60": must be 1 to 30 (login.maxBackoffSeconds is 30)`.

A bad line in an address list is named by its position, counting from 0: `key "access.allow[0]" has invalid value "10.0.0.1": want CIDR such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 192.0.2.7/32 (...)`, or `use the IPv4 form` for an IPv6-mapped address.

#### An allow list that would lock you out

- `This allow list would deny your own address (10.0.4.17). Add it, or a range that contains it.`
- `The gateway cannot tell your address, so this allow list would deny this browser.`

#### Other refusals

| The page says | Why, and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| A dialog: `This settings page was changed by someone else since you opened it.` with **Reload** | Another administrator saved first. **Reload** shows their settings and drops your changes. Cancel, <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a click outside leaves the dialog and keeps your edits on the page, but they cannot be saved until you reload. |
| `config.yaml was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | See the next section. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | The audit setting above is on **Refuse changes until it can be written**, and the audit log is failing. Fix the disk on the gateway host. |
| `The gateway could not write its data files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The settings file could not be written. Check the gateway's data volume on its host. |
| `The gateway cannot read config.yaml (<cause>). The cause is on the gateway host; once the gateway can read the file again, reload this page.` | The page shows this when it loads the settings, instead of the settings, with the cause the gateway found in place of `<cause>`. Reload once the gateway can read the file. |
| `The page did not send the version it was working from, so the gateway refused the change. Reload the page and try again.` | Press **Reload**, make your change again and save. |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | Your session ended. The page signs you out; sign in again. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | Your account is not an administrator. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway is limiting requests. Wait, then save again. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` or `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | The request may or may not have arrived. Press **Reload** to see what the gateway holds. |

### When the settings file was changed on the host

The gateway writes its settings to a file, `config.yaml`, in its data volume. It never expects anyone to change that file. If it is changed on the gateway host while the gateway runs, the page shows a banner:

> [!IMPORTANT]
> `config.yaml was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit; saving here is blocked until then.`

**Save** is off while the banner shows. The gateway holds to the settings it loaded, and it will not save over a change it has not read. Press **Restart gateway** to make it read the file, then make your changes. A refused save also brings the banner up.

The users store, the connections store and the store key have no setting: they always live in the gateway's `/data` folder. **Backup & Restore** is how you move them to another gateway.

### Restarting the gateway

The **Gateway** card at the foot of the page holds one button, **Restart gateway**. It makes the gateway start its program again, in place, with the same arguments and environment. You rarely need it: settings apply when you save them. Use it to make the gateway read a settings file that was changed on its host.

![The Gateway card with the Restart gateway button and its progress line, above the confirmation dialog with Cancel and Restart gateway.](../src/modules/gateway-settings/help/restart.svg)

*Figure 3. The Gateway card, and the question the button asks.*

1. **Restart gateway**.
2. The progress line, which appears once the gateway has accepted the request.
3. The question the dialog asks.
4. **Cancel**. Nothing happens.
5. **Restart gateway** in the dialog. It starts the restart.

1. Press **Restart gateway**. The page asks `Restart the gateway? Everyone is signed out and open broker connections close. It is back in a few seconds.`
2. Press **Restart gateway** in the dialog. **Cancel**, <kbd>Esc</kbd> or a click outside restarts nothing.
3. The button goes off and the page says `Restarting the gateway. This page goes to the sign-in when the gateway answers again.`
4. When the gateway answers again, the page reloads and takes you to the sign-in.

> [!WARNING]
> A restart signs out everyone, you included, and closes every open broker connection. Warn people first.

The page looks for the gateway once a second, for a minute. If it has not answered by then, the progress line goes and the page says `The gateway has not answered after a minute. Check it on its host, then reload this page.` The button comes back on. If the gateway does not accept the request, the page shows the reason in red under the button.

A restart uses the environment the gateway already has. A change to a variable the operator sets, such as where the gateway finds its certificate, needs the container made again: see the [Restart gateway](provisioned-mode.md#restart-gateway) section of the Provisioned mode guide.

---

## Certificates

See the certificate the gateway presents to browsers and the CA certificates it trusts when it connects to brokers. Where the gateway's files allow it, replace the certificate and add or delete trusted CAs.

Certificates is a page of the administration app, which the gateway serves at `/solAdmin` to administrators only. It needs an administrator's session. Without one, the page shows **Administrator Sign-in Required** and the line `Sign in as an administrator to see or change the gateway's certificates.` in place of everything below. How the gateway's certificate files are mounted, and how an operator locks them, is in the [operator's guide](provisioned-mode.md#certificates-from-the-console).

A change made here applies at once and needs no restart. The gateway's files are named by its environment, never on this page.

### The page at a glance

The page is an introduction card and three more cards: **Gateway certificate** (which also holds the **Replace certificate** form), **Trusted broker CAs** (which also holds the **Add CA certificate** form) and **Standard root CAs**.

![The Certificates page: the introduction with a Reload button, the Gateway certificate card with its details, the Replace certificate form, the Trusted broker CAs card with one file and the Add CA certificate form, and the Standard root CAs card.](../src/modules/tls-certificates/help/page.svg)

*Figure 1. The Certificates page, with a gateway certificate that ends in nine days.*

1. **Reload** reads the certificate and the trusted CAs from the gateway again.
2. What the page shows about the gateway's own certificate: **Subject**, **Names**, **Issuer**, **Valid from**, **Valid to** and **Fingerprint (SHA-256)**.
3. The mark after **Valid to**: **Expired**, or **Expires in N days** when 30 days or fewer remain.
4. The note shown for a self-signed certificate.
5. The **Certificate file** and **Key file** choosers.
6. The **Certificate (PEM)** and **Private key (PEM)** boxes, for pasting text instead of choosing a file.
7. **Replace certificate** checks the pair, then installs it once you confirm.
8. A trusted CA file, with the certificates it holds and its **Delete** button.
9. The **Add CA certificate** form: a file chooser, a PEM box, an optional file name and the **Add CA certificate** button.
10. The standard root CAs the gateway carries, whether they are trusted, and a list of them.

The red lines on the page are refusals: one under the introduction, one in each form and one above the trusted CA list. They are listed under Refusals below. A red line clears when you start the next action.

### Reading the gateway certificate

The **Gateway certificate** card describes the certificate the gateway presents to browsers and to every client that connects to it. It shows the leaf certificate only: the first certificate of a chain.

| Line | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Subject** | Who the certificate is issued to, with every attribute in the certificate's order, as `openssl` prints it: `CN=gateway.example.org, O=Example`. |
| **Names** | The DNS names, then the IP addresses, that the certificate covers, one to a line. `None listed` when it names none. |
| **Issuer** | Who signed it, in the same form as the subject. |
| **Valid from** | The start of its validity, in UTC. |
| **Valid to** | The end of its validity, in UTC, with the expiry mark when one applies. |
| **Fingerprint (SHA-256)** | The SHA-256 fingerprint as hex pairs. Compare it with the fingerprint your certificate authority gave you. |

When the certificate's subject and issuer are the same, the card adds a note: `This certificate is self-signed (the gateway makes one for itself at first start). Browsers warn about it until it is replaced with one they trust.`

### Expiry marks

A mark follows the **Valid to** time of every certificate the page lists: the gateway's own, the one in the preview of a replacement, every certificate in a trusted CA file and every standard root CA.

- **Expired** (red) when the end of validity has passed.
- **Expires in N days** (amber) when 30 days or fewer remain, counted up to the next whole day. It reads **Expires in 1 day** for the last day.
- No mark when more than 30 days remain.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The page does not renew anything and does not send a reminder. Look at **Valid to** from time to time. A self-signed certificate that the gateway made for itself at first start lasts seven days and is never renewed, so replace it soon after the first start.

### Replacing the gateway certificate

You need two things from your certificate authority: the certificate (it may carry its chain, leaf first) and its private key without a passphrase. The gateway checks the pair before it writes anything.

![The Replace certificate form after a successful check: the file choosers, the certificate box with PEM text, the key box shown as dots, the preview of what will be installed and the Replace certificate button.](../src/modules/tls-certificates/help/replace.svg)

*Figure 2. A pair that the gateway accepted. The key is drawn as dots here; the page does not show it back.*

1. The **Certificate file** and **Key file** choosers.
2. The **Certificate (PEM)** and **Private key (PEM)** boxes. Whatever is in these boxes is what the page sends.
3. The preview: `The gateway accepted the pair. This is what will be installed:`, with the details of the certificate.
4. **Replace certificate**.

1. Choose the **Certificate file** (`.crt`, `.pem` or `.cer`) and the **Key file** (`.key` or `.pem`). The page reads each file into the box beside it. Or paste the PEM text into **Certificate (PEM)** and **Private key (PEM)**.
2. Press **Replace certificate**. The gateway checks the pair and writes nothing yet. If it refuses, a red line under the boxes says why; see Refusals below.
3. Read the preview on the page behind the box. Look at **Names**: the gateway does not compare them with the address people use to reach it.
4. A box asks the question below, with the subject, the end of validity and the fingerprint of the certificate. Press **Install** to go on, or **Cancel** to stop. The preview closes when you answer.
5. The toast `Certificate replaced. New connections use it now.` appears, and the card shows the certificate you installed.

![The confirmation box that asks whether to install the certificate, with its Cancel and Install buttons.](../src/modules/tls-certificates/help/install.svg)

*Figure 3. The question before the certificate goes live.*

1. The question: `Install this certificate?`, with the subject, the end of validity and the fingerprint, and what happens next.
2. **Cancel** leaves the certificate as it is.
3. **Install** replaces it.

#### What the gateway checks

The same checks run when you press **Replace certificate** and again when you press **Install**, so a certificate that expires in between is still refused.

- The certificate box holds certificates only: at least one, no key, no other kind of block and no text after the last block.
- The key box holds exactly one private key, without a passphrase, in a kind the gateway supports: RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519.
- The key matches the first certificate.
- The first certificate is valid today: not expired and already started.
- The certificate's own key is one that browsers can use: RSA of at least 2048 bits, or ECDSA on P-256 or P-384. An Ed25519 certificate is refused here, although an Ed25519 key is otherwise accepted. The gateway serves the new certificate at once, so a certificate that browsers refuse would lock you out of this page.

#### What happens to your key

The page sends the key once and keeps no copy. The gateway writes it to its key file and nowhere else: it does not echo it, log it or write it to the audit trail. The **Private key (PEM)** box and the **Key file** chooser are emptied after every attempt, whether it succeeds, is refused or is cancelled. The certificate box is emptied only after a successful replacement, so after a refusal you can fix the key and try again.

#### What applies at once

Connections to the gateway made from then on present the installed certificate. Connections already open carry on with the old one until they close. The gateway keeps the certificate and the key in its files, so they are still in place after a restart. Each replacement is written to the audit trail with the subject and the end of validity.

### Reading the trusted broker CAs

The **Trusted broker CAs** card lists the files the gateway reads when it checks a broker's certificate: every `.crt` and `.pem` file in its trust folder, by name. Under each name the card lists the certificates in the file, one to a line, as `subject: valid to time; SHA-256 fingerprint`, with the expiry mark when one applies. A file may hold several certificates.

A file that gives no certificate says why in red: `No certificate from this file: The file holds no certificate.` or `No certificate from this file: The file cannot be read.` When the folder holds no such file, the card says `No CA files in the trust directory.`

![The Trusted broker CAs card: one CA file with an Expired mark, one file that holds no certificate, and the Add CA certificate form with a file chooser, a PEM box, a file name and a refusal in red.](../src/modules/tls-certificates/help/trust.svg)

*Figure 4. Two files in the list, and the form that adds a third.*

1. A file whose certificate has expired: the file name, its **Delete** button, the certificate line and the **Expired** mark.
2. A file that holds no certificate, with the reason in red.
3. The **CA certificate file** chooser.
4. The **CA certificate (PEM)** box.
5. The **File name (optional)** field.
6. A refusal from the form.
7. The **Add CA certificate** button.

### Adding a trusted CA

1. Choose a **CA certificate file** (`.crt`, `.pem` or `.cer`), or paste the text into **CA certificate (PEM)**.
2. If you want to name the file, type the name in **File name (optional)**. The rules are in the table below.
3. Press **Add CA certificate**.
4. The toast `CA certificate added. New broker connections trust it now.` appears, the three boxes are emptied and the file is in the list.

| Field | What it is | What it accepts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CA certificate file** | A file the page reads into the box below it. | A file of 64 KiB or less. |
| **CA certificate (PEM)** | The certificates to trust. | One or more certificate blocks and nothing else: a private key is refused, and so is any text after the last block. Required. |
| **File name (optional)** | The name of the file the gateway writes. | Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores. It starts with a letter or a digit, ends in `.crt` or `.pem` in lower case, and has at most 64 characters before the extension. Left empty, the gateway names the file after the common name of the first certificate: lower case, every run of other characters turned into one dash, dashes at both ends dropped, then `.crt` (`ca.crt` when nothing is left). |

The gateway never writes over a file. A name that is already in the list is refused: delete that file first, or choose another name. The certificates in the file are trusted by the next connection the gateway makes to a broker.

### Deleting a trusted CA

1. Press **Delete** on the file's row.
2. Read the question: `Delete "east-prod-ca.pem" from the trusted CAs? Brokers that rely on it stop verifying for new connections at once.`
3. Press **Delete** to confirm, or **Cancel**. The toast reads `Deleted east-prod-ca.pem` and the file leaves the list.

> [!WARNING]
> A deleted file cannot be brought back from this page. A broker whose certificate chains only to a CA in that file, and not to a standard root CA that is trusted, fails to verify on its next connection until you add the CA again. Connections already open carry on.

Delete works on every file the list shows, including a file that someone placed in the folder by hand.

### The standard root CAs

The **Standard root CAs** card describes the public root CAs that the gateway's image carries, from Mozilla's list. The page cannot add or delete them: they come with the image and change with a new release, unless whoever runs the gateway mounts the host's CA bundle in place of the image's list. The gateway then trusts what the host trusts, and reads it at every start. That is set up outside these pages: see [Trusting the host's CA store](deployment.md#trusting-the-hosts-ca-store). Whether the gateway trusts them is a setting, **Trust the standard root CAs**, on the Gateway Settings page (see the Gateway Settings chapter).

- When they are on, the card says `Trusted: brokers whose certificates chain to one of these N certificates are accepted.`
- When they are off, it says `Not trusted: turned off on Gateway Settings. Only the CA files above are trusted.`
- **Show the N certificates** opens the list, sorted by subject, in the same form as the trusted CA files. It is absent when the gateway read none.
- When the gateway read none, a red line says why: `The gateway image holds no standard root CA bundle.`, `The standard root CA bundle cannot be read.` or `The standard root CA bundle holds no certificate.` Only the CA files above are trusted then. When the standard root CAs are on, the status line still reads `Trusted`, with `0 certificates`.

### When the certificates are locked

Whether the page may change the files is decided by how the operator mounted them, not by a setting on this page. When the gateway cannot write them, the page still shows everything, but it says so and disables the controls. The certificate and the trusted CAs are judged separately.

![The Certificates page with its files locked: a warning line under the gateway certificate, a warning line over the trusted CAs, and the Replace certificate, Delete and Add CA certificate buttons greyed out.](../src/modules/tls-certificates/help/locked.svg)

*Figure 5. Both sets of files locked, and the standard root CAs turned off with no bundle to read.*

1. `The certificate files are read-only on the gateway host, so the certificate cannot be replaced here.`
2. **Replace certificate**, the file choosers and the PEM boxes of the form are disabled.
3. `The trust files are read-only on the gateway host, so CA certificates cannot be added or deleted here.`
4. Every **Delete** button is disabled.
5. The **Add CA certificate** form is disabled.
6. The status of the standard root CAs, here `Not trusted: turned off on Gateway Settings. Only the CA files above are trusted.`
7. The reason the gateway read no standard root CAs.

The certificate is locked when its folder is not writable, and also when the certificate and its key are in two different folders. A locked certificate changes on the gateway host: the operator replaces the files and restarts the gateway. Ask the operator, or read how the files are locked and unlocked in the [operator's guide](provisioned-mode.md#locking-them).

If the files turn read-only while the page is open, the action is refused with the message below and the page reloads, so it shows the banners and the disabled controls.

### Refusals

A refusal appears as a red line: under the introduction when the page cannot load, under the form for a replacement or an addition, and above the list for a deletion. The gateway's own words are shown as they are.

#### Before anything is sent

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Choose a certificate file or paste the certificate (PEM).` | Fill the certificate box. |
| `Choose a key file or paste the private key (PEM).` | Fill the key box. |
| `Choose a CA certificate file or paste the certificate (PEM).` | Fill the CA certificate box. |
| `name is larger than 64 KiB, the most the gateway accepts in one request.` (with the file's name in front) | A file chosen in any of the three choosers is larger than one request can carry. The page does not read it. Use a smaller file. |
| `The certificate and key together are larger than the 64 KiB the gateway accepts in one request. Leave out any certificate the chain does not need.` | Remove certificates from the chain that the gateway does not need, such as the root. |
| `This CA file is larger than the 64 KiB the gateway accepts in one request. Split it into smaller files and add each one.` | Add the certificates in several files. |

#### From the certificate checks

| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `No certificate was found. Send the PEM text, from -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- to -----END CERTIFICATE-----.` | The certificate box has no certificate block. |
| `A private key was found. A private key never belongs here: send only the certificate.` | A key is in a certificate box, for the gateway or for a CA. |
| `A "TYPE" block was found. Only CERTIFICATE blocks are accepted.` | The text holds another kind of block. The message names the kind in place of TYPE. |
| `A CERTIFICATE block cannot be read as a certificate.` | The text is damaged or cut short. |
| `There is text after the last certificate block. Send only certificate blocks.` | Delete what follows the last `-----END CERTIFICATE-----` line. |
| `No private key was found. Send the PEM text, from -----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY----- to -----END PRIVATE KEY-----.` | The key box has no key block. |
| `The key is encrypted. Send it without a passphrase (openssl pkey -in key.pem -out plain.pem).` | Remove the passphrase first, with the command the message names. |
| `A "TYPE" block was found. Only the private key belongs here.` | The key box holds another kind of block, for example the certificate. |
| `More than one private key was found. Send exactly one.` | Keep one key. |
| `There is text after the key block. Send only the key.` | Delete what follows the key block. |
| `The key does not match the certificate (the first one sent).` | The key belongs to another certificate. The first certificate in the box must be the leaf. |
| `The private key cannot be read, or is a kind the gateway does not support. Use an RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519 key.` | The key text is damaged, or the key is of another kind. |
| `The certificate expired on 2026-11-01T09:00:00Z.` | The certificate's end of validity has passed. The message gives it in UTC. Get a renewed certificate. |
| `The certificate is not valid until 2026-12-01T09:00:00Z.` | The certificate has not started yet. The message gives its start in UTC. |
| `The certificate's key is ECDSA on P-521, which Chrome and Edge cannot use for TLS. Issue the certificate for an RSA key of at least 2048 bits, or an ECDSA key on P-256 or P-384.` | The gateway refuses a certificate that browsers cannot use. The first part of the message changes with the key: `RSA with N bits, which browsers refuse` for an RSA key under 2048 bits, and `Ed25519, which browsers do not accept in a TLS certificate`. |

#### From the file name and the files

| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, start with a letter or digit, end in .crt or .pem, and keep the name before the extension to 64 characters.` | The **File name (optional)** breaks the rules in the table above. |
| `A CA file with that name already exists. Delete it first, or choose another name.` | The name is in the list. |
| `Not found. It may already have been removed.` | A **Delete** found the file gone, for example because another administrator deleted it. The list reloads. |
| `The gateway's certificate or trust files are read-only on its host, so they cannot be changed here.` | The files are locked. See the section above. |
| `The gateway could not write its certificate or trust files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | The write failed, for example on a full disk. Nothing changed. Ask the operator to read the gateway's log. |

#### From the session and the gateway

| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | Shown as a toast, and the app signs you out. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | The session is not an administrator's. |
| `You must change your password before you continue.` | The administrator's password must be changed first. |
| `The gateway rejected the request as malformed.` | The gateway could not read what the page sent. |
| `The gateway refused a cross-site request.` | The page was not opened from the gateway's own address. |
| `The request is too large.` | The gateway refused the size of the request. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway is limiting how often you call it. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway is set to refuse changes while its audit trail cannot be written, and a certificate or CA change is a change. Checking a certificate and reading the page still work. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` | The page cannot reach the gateway. Check the connection and press **Reload**. |
| `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | Press **Reload** and look at the page before you repeat a change. |
| `The gateway sent a response this page cannot read.` | Something between you and the gateway answered in its place. Press **Reload**. |

---

## Backup & Restore

Keep a copy of the gateway's users, connections and settings, and bring one back. You can export a copy by hand, restore from a file, and let the gateway write a backup on a schedule.

Backup & Restore is part of the administration app at `/solAdmin`, and it needs an administrator's session. Without one the page shows **Administrator Sign-in Required**, with the line `Sign in as an administrator to back up or restore the gateway configuration.` in place of everything below. If your session ends or you lose your administrator rights while the page is open, it clears the passphrases you typed and the file you chose, and shows the same card.

### What a backup holds

A backup is one file, sealed with a passphrase that you choose. It holds three things:

- **Users.** Each user as the gateway stores them, with the hash of the password, never the password itself. A user's two-factor secret and the hashes of the unused recovery codes are part of the record.
- **Connections.** Each connection with its credentials: the SEMP and the Message VPN passwords.
- **Settings.** The gateway settings, except the file paths. The paths of the certificate, the key and the trusted CAs come from the gateway's host and are not in a backup.

A backup does not hold the audit trail, the queues or messages on your brokers, or a session. It opens on any gateway, whatever that gateway's own keys are. The passphrase is the only key: without it, nobody can open the file, and the gateway cannot tell it to you.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Treat a backup and its passphrase like the broker credentials themselves. With both, someone holds every user's password hash and every connection's credentials. Keep the passphrase apart from the file.

### The page at a glance

The page has two cards. **Configuration** exports and imports by hand. **Schedule** sets the backups the gateway writes by itself, and lists the files they leave.

![The Backup and Restore page: a Configuration card with an Export form and an Import form, and a Schedule card with a status line, the schedule form, three buttons and a list of saved backups.](../src/modules/backup/help/page.svg)

*Figure 1. Backup & Restore: the Configuration card above, the Schedule card below.*

1. Export: a passphrase, its confirmation and the **Export** button.
2. Import: the backup file, its passphrase and the **Preview** button.
3. **Reload** reads the schedule and the saved backups from the gateway again.
4. The status of the schedule: when it runs, when it runs next, and the last backup.
5. The schedule form: how often, when, how many backups to keep, and the passphrase.
6. **Save schedule**, **Back up now** and **Remove schedule**.
7. **Saved backups**: the files in the gateway's backup directory, each with a download icon and a restore icon.

### Exporting a backup

Use **Export** to take a copy of the configuration as it stands, for example before a change or before you replace the gateway. The copy is a file that your browser saves.

1. Type a passphrase in **Passphrase (12 to 128 characters)**. It must be 12 to 128 characters long.
2. Type the same passphrase in **Confirm the passphrase**.
3. Press **Export**. Your browser saves a file named like `smu-backup-20261122T020000Z.json`: the date and time of the export in UTC. A toast says `Exported` followed by the file name.

After a successful export the page clears both passphrase fields. It keeps no passphrase: each action sends the one you typed for it.

If the two fields differ, the page says `The passphrases do not match.` and sends nothing. If the passphrase is shorter than 12 or longer than 128 characters, the gateway refuses with `The passphrase must be 12 to 128 characters.`

### Restoring from a file

Restoring is two steps. **Preview** opens the file and shows what an import would change, and changes nothing. You then choose, for each part, what to import, and press **Import**.

![The Import form after a preview: the chosen file, the date and gateway version of the backup, a choice and a list of changes for users, connections and settings, a warning about signing out, and the Import button.](../src/modules/backup/help/preview.svg)

*Figure 2. The Import form after a preview, with one choice for each part of the backup.*

1. The file, its passphrase and **Preview**. Under the file box the page names what you chose.
2. When the backup was made and by which gateway version.
3. One choice for **Users**, **Connections** and **Settings**.
4. What importing that part would add, change and remove.
5. The warning that the import signs you out.
6. **Import** applies the choices.

1. Under **Backup file**, choose a file. The box takes a `.json` file of at most 8 MiB, the most the gateway accepts in one import. The page then shows `File:` and the file's name. To restore a backup the gateway wrote itself, use its restore icon in **Saved backups** instead: the page then shows `Saved backup:` and the name, and puts the cursor in the passphrase box.
2. Type the passphrase the backup was sealed with in **Passphrase**. For a saved backup, that is the passphrase of the schedule when the file was written.
3. Press **Preview**. The gateway opens the file and the page shows when the backup was made, by which gateway, and a list of changes for each part. Choosing another file hides the preview.
4. For each of **Users**, **Connections** and **Settings**, read the list and choose what to do. Every choice starts at **Skip**.
5. Press **Import**. The page asks you to confirm, naming the parts you chose, for example `Import users (merge), settings (replace) from this backup? The gateway applies it at once.` Press **Import** in that box to go on, or cancel.

#### The choices

| Part | Choice | What the gateway does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Users, Connections | **Skip** | Leaves the part as it is. |
| Users, Connections | **Merge: add and update these, keep the others** | Adds the backup's records, and replaces any record that has the same name. Records that the backup does not hold stay. Users are matched by user name, connections by broker name. |
| Users | **Replace: these users only** | Makes the user list exactly the backup's. A user the backup does not hold is removed. |
| Connections | **Replace: these connections only** | Makes the connection list exactly the backup's. A connection the backup does not hold is removed. |
| Settings | **Skip** or **Replace** | Replaces every setting with the backup's. There is no merge for settings. |

The list under each choice has up to three kinds of line: `Add:` names that are not there yet, `Change:` names whose record differs, and `Remove (Replace only):` names that only **Replace** would delete. For settings the line is `Change:` and the settings keys that differ, such as `logLevel`. A part with nothing to do says `No change.`

The gateway imports the parts you chose together, or none of them. If one of them is refused, nothing is imported.

> [!WARNING]
> An import overwrites what the gateway holds, at once, and there is no undo.
>
> - **Replace** for users or connections deletes every record that the backup does not hold, and every record it does hold takes the backup's values, passwords and permissions included.
> - **Replace** for settings overwrites all the settings, and they apply to the running gateway at once.
> - Export a backup first if you may want to return to what the gateway holds today.

#### Sessions and two-factor after a restore

An import ends the sessions of the users it changes in these ways: the user is removed, or the backup changes their password hash or whether they are an administrator, or it adds, removes or replaces their two-factor secret. Those users sign in again. A change to the recovery codes alone does not end a session. A user the import adds has no session to end.

Two-factor is restored as the file holds it. A user whose record in the backup has no two-factor ends up without it, and a user whose record has it ends up with the secret and the unused recovery codes in the file. An import changes nothing else about two-factor. A backup without the two-factor mode reads as `optional`, so importing its settings with **Replace** sets the mode to `optional`: check the mode afterwards; the Gateway Settings chapter describes it.

When the import would change your own account, a banner appears under the users choice: `Importing the users this way changes your own account: you will be signed out.` It shows only for the users choice that would do this: **Merge** and **Replace** are checked separately. After such an import a toast says `Imported. Your own account changed: sign in again.` and the app signs you out. After any other import the toast says `Imported`, and the page clears the file and the passphrase and reloads the schedule.

The backup's settings and the way it treats two-factor are described for the operator in [Backups and two-factor](provisioned-mode.md#backups-and-two-factor).

#### When the data changes during a preview

The preview is a picture of the gateway at one moment. If anyone changes the users, the connections or the settings (a password change counts) after the preview, and before you press **Import**, the gateway refuses the import for the parts that changed. The page hides the preview and says `The gateway's data changed since the preview. Run the preview again.` The file and passphrase stay filled in. Press **Preview** again, read the list and choose again.

### Scheduled backups

The gateway can write a backup by itself. Each one is sealed with the schedule's passphrase, so nobody has to be signed in. The gateway writes the files into its backup directory, which the operator mounts from the host so that the files stay outside the container. The operator's side is in [Back up and restore](provisioned-mode.md#back-up-and-restore). All times on this card are UTC.

![The Schedule card with a weekly schedule: the status lines, the frequency, day and time, the number of backups to keep, the passphrase fields, three buttons and two saved backups with a download and a restore icon each.](../src/modules/backup/help/schedule.svg)

*Figure 3. The Schedule card for a weekly schedule, with two saved backups.*

1. The status: the schedule in words, the next run and the last backup.
2. How often, and when.
3. **Backups to keep**.
4. The passphrase and its confirmation.
5. **Save schedule**, **Back up now** and **Remove schedule**.
6. The list of saved backups.
7. The download icon and the restore icon of one backup.

#### The status

Above the form the page tells you where the schedule stands:

- With no schedule: `No schedule: the gateway writes no backups until you save one.`
- With one: the schedule in words, such as `Weekly on Monday at 02:15 UTC; keeps the last 14.`, then `Next backup:` and the time.
- After a run: `Last backup:` the file name and the time, or `Last backup,` the time, `failed:` and the reason. The gateway keeps the last run in memory, so a restart of the gateway clears it.

When the gateway cannot write to its backup directory, a banner under the heading says why. The reason is one of these:

- `/backup does not exist. Mount a directory there to keep backups outside the container.`
- `/backup is not a directory. Mount a directory there.`
- `Cannot read /backup:` and the system's reason.
- `/backup is not writable`, followed by a hint about who owns the directory when the gateway can tell.

While the directory has a problem the list of saved backups says `The backup directory cannot be read.` Fix it on the host; the operator's guide shows how. **Reload** checks again.

#### Setting the schedule

1. Choose **Frequency**. The fields below change with it (see the table).
2. Set when the backup runs, in UTC.
3. Set **Backups to keep**.
4. Type the passphrase twice. A schedule that does not exist yet needs one. When you edit a schedule, leave both boxes blank to keep the current passphrase, or type another to change it.
5. Press **Save schedule**. A toast says `Schedule saved`, the page clears the passphrase boxes, and the status shows the next run.

| Field | Shown for | What it takes | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Frequency** | Every schedule | **Hourly**, **Daily**, **Weekly** or **Monthly**. | Daily |
| **Minute past the hour** | Hourly | A whole number from 0 to 59. | 0 |
| **Time (UTC)** | Daily, weekly and monthly | A time of day, in UTC. | 02:00 |
| **Day of the week** | Weekly | Sunday to Saturday. | Sunday |
| **Day of the month** | Monthly | A whole number from 1 to 31. A month without that day backs up on its last day. | 1 |
| **Backups to keep** | Every schedule | A whole number from 1 to 365. After each backup the gateway deletes the oldest ones beyond this number. | 14 |
| **Passphrase** and **Confirm the passphrase** | Every schedule | 12 to 128 characters, the same in both boxes. Under the box the page says `Required: every scheduled backup is encrypted with it.` when there is no schedule, and `Leave blank to keep the current passphrase.` when there is one. | Empty |

The gateway lists and deletes only the files it wrote itself, named like `smu-backup-20261122T020000Z.json`. It leaves any other file in the directory alone. A change of passphrase applies to the backups written from then on. The files already saved stay sealed with the passphrase they were written with.

#### Running a backup now

Press **Back up now** to write a backup at once, with the saved schedule and its passphrase. Edits you have made in the form but not saved do not count, and they stay in the form. The button is greyed out while there is no schedule. A toast says `Backup written:` and the file name, and the status and the list refresh. If the gateway cannot write the file, the reason shows above the buttons and the status line records the failed run. Two backups made in the same second would share a name, so a second press within a second can fail with a message that asks you to wait a second and run it again.

#### Removing the schedule

Press **Remove schedule** to stop the scheduled backups. A box asks `Remove the backup schedule? The saved backups stay.` Press **Remove** to go on. A toast says `Schedule removed`. The files in the backup directory stay where they are. The button is greyed out while there is no schedule.

#### Saved backups

The list shows the files the gateway has written, newest first: **File**, **Created (UTC)** and **Size**. Each row ends with two icons:

- The download icon, named `Download "file name"` when you point at it. Your browser saves the file as the gateway wrote it. It is still sealed with the schedule's passphrase.
- The restore icon, named `Restore "file name"`. It fills the Import form in the Configuration card with this backup, so that you only type the passphrase and press **Preview**. See Restoring from a file, above.

With no files the list says `No saved backups yet.` The page offers no way to delete a single backup. The gateway deletes the oldest ones itself, as **Backups to keep** says.

**Reload** fetches the schedule and the list again. It also fills the schedule fields with the saved schedule, so use it to drop edits you have not saved.

#### When another administrator changes the schedule

Two administrators can edit the schedule at the same time. The gateway keeps the first save and refuses the second, so that nobody overwrites a change they never saw:

- If the schedule changed since you opened it, a box says `This schedule was changed by someone else since you opened it.` Press **Reload** to see the current schedule, or cancel to keep your edits.
- If you save a first schedule but another administrator saved one before you, the page says `Someone else saved a schedule since you opened this page. It is shown now; change it if you still want to.` and shows theirs.
- If another administrator removed the schedule, a toast says `This schedule was deleted by someone else.` and the page reloads.

### Refusals and messages

A refusal shows in red in the card it belongs to: under the Export form, under the Import form (above **Preview**), above the schedule buttons, or, for loading and downloading, under the heading of the Schedule card.

#### Export and import

| Message | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `The passphrases do not match.` | The two passphrase boxes differ. Type the same text in both. |
| `The passphrase must be 12 to 128 characters.` | The passphrase is too short or too long. Applies to an export, to a schedule, and to opening a file. |
| `Choose a backup file, or a saved backup below.` | You pressed **Preview** with no file chosen. |
| `smu-backup-20261122T020000Z.json is larger than the 8 MiB the gateway accepts in one import.` | The file you chose, whose name the message gives, is too big. A real backup is far smaller: check that you chose the right file. |
| `This is not a Solace Message Utility backup file.` | The file is not a backup made by this application. |
| `This backup file is damaged.` | The file is cut short or has been edited. Use another copy. |
| `This backup has format version N, which this gateway does not read.` | The file's format is one this gateway cannot open. N is the file's version. |
| `The passphrase does not open this file, or the file is damaged.` | Check the passphrase, letter case included. If it is right, the file is damaged. |
| `There is no backup named "name".` | A saved backup you chose is not in the backup directory. Press **Reload** and choose from the list. |
| `Choose at least one section to import.` | All three choices are **Skip**. Choose **Merge** or **Replace** for at least one. |
| `The backup's users cannot be imported:` a reason | The users in the backup break a rule the gateway applies to its own users. The reason says which. The same holds for `The backup's connections cannot be imported:`. |
| `At least one administrator must remain.` | The users you chose would leave the gateway with no administrator. Choose **Merge**, or use a backup that holds an administrator. |
| `This allow list would deny your own address (203.0.113.7). Add it, or a range that contains it.` | The backup's settings carry an access list that would lock your browser out. The gateway gives a similar reason, `The gateway cannot tell your address, so this allow list would deny this browser.`, when it cannot tell your address. Choose **Skip** for the settings and import the other parts. |
| A reason about a setting | The gateway refuses settings that it would not accept at start, for example settings that would turn Provisioned mode off. The reason says which setting and why. Choose **Skip** for the settings. |
| `The gateway's data changed since the preview. Run the preview again.` | See "When the data changes during a preview", above. |

#### Schedule

| Message | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter a time.` | The time box is empty. Give a time of day. |
| `Enter whole numbers.` | A minute, a day of the month or **Backups to keep** is empty or not a whole number. |
| `The minute must be 0 to 59.` | The minute is out of range. |
| `The day of the month must be 1 to 31, and only a monthly schedule takes one.` | The day of the month is out of range. |
| `Keep 1 to 365 backups.` | **Backups to keep** is out of range. |
| `A new schedule needs a passphrase.` | You saved a schedule that does not exist yet with the passphrase boxes blank. Type a passphrase. |
| A reason that names a file or the directory, such as `already exists; wait a second and run it again` | A run failed, and the message is the gateway's own reason. Read it, fix the cause (often the backup directory), and press **Back up now** again. The gateway's log has the detail. |

#### Any action

| Message | What it means and what to do |
| --- | --- |
| `Your session has ended. Sign in again.` | The gateway ended your session. The message is a toast, and the app returns to the sign-in. |
| `You must change your password before you continue.` | Your own password is due for a change. Change it on the gateway's sign-in page, then return. |
| `This needs an administrator.` | Your account does not have administrator rights. |
| `The gateway rejected the request as malformed.` | The gateway could not read what the page sent. Reload the page and try again. |
| `The gateway refused a cross-site request.` | The page was opened from another address than the gateway's own. Open `/solAdmin` on the gateway's address and try again. |
| `Not found. It may already have been removed.` | What you asked for is not there, for example a saved backup that has been deleted since the list loaded. Press **Reload**. |
| `Too many requests. Wait a minute and try again.` | The gateway refused because requests came too fast. Wait a minute. |
| `The request is too large.` | The request is larger than the gateway accepts. |
| `This was changed by someone else since you opened it. Reload to see the current version.` | Another administrator saved first. Press **Reload**. |
| `The page did not send the version it was working from, so the gateway refused the change. Reload the page and try again.` | Reload the page. |
| `A data file (users, connections or backup settings) was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | A file on the gateway's host was changed outside these pages. The operator must restart the gateway before the change can go through. |
| `config.yaml was edited on the gateway host since the gateway loaded it. Restart the gateway to load that edit, then make your change here.` | The same, for the settings file. It can appear when you import settings. |
| `The gateway cannot read its config.yaml. Its log has the cause.` | The gateway cannot read its settings file. Tell the operator. |
| `The gateway could not write its data files, so nothing was changed. Its log has the cause.` | Nothing was imported or saved. Tell the operator. |
| `The gateway cannot write its audit log and is set to refuse changes until it can. Its log has the cause.` | An import or a schedule change is refused while the audit log cannot be written. Tell the operator. |
| `The gateway could not complete the request. Its log has the cause.` | An error inside the gateway. Tell the operator. |
| `The gateway sent a response this page cannot read.` | Something between your browser and the gateway answered in place of it. Try again, and tell the operator if it persists. |
| `The gateway could not be reached.` | The page could not contact the gateway. Check your network and try again. |
| `The gateway did not answer in time. If this was a change, it may still have been applied: reload to see where it stands before you try again.` | Press **Reload** and check before you repeat an import or a save. |
